data.title: Sony's Mark Cerny Has Worked on "Big Chunks of RDNA 5" with AMD
data.author: ZenithExtreme
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：PlayStation与AMD的合作及其技术前景

不同观点：
• basfo认为，当前所有游戏主机本质上都是PC，只是前端和商店不同，且随着Xbox开始开放，PlayStation可能也会跟随。
• phkahler建议直接引用相关文章，提供更多背景信息。
• DiabloD3指出，RDNA5并不在路线图上，接下来的重点是UDNA1，这是一种与CDNA融合的架构，尽管一些文章标题可能引起误解。
• whatever1提到，PS5相对于PS4 Pro的性能提升并不如以前世代明显，现在的图形改进需要更多的计算能力，或者游戏引擎变得过于臃肿。
• georgeecollins对Mark Cerny给予高度评价，并认为Sony作为一个公司，能够让一位美国出生的游戏开发者（工程师）担任重要职位，显示了其开放和尊重专业的态度。
• LorenDB认为，如果PlayStation的贡献足够好，RDNA4到RDNA5的改进可能和RDNA3到RDNA4一样显著，只要价格合理。
• erulabs对UDNA1的软件支持表示期待，希望AMD能在数据中心领域与Nvidia展开真正竞争，但也担心AMD如果再次在驱动和支持上出问题，可能会影响其声誉。
• monster_truck指出，AMD与Sony在FSR 3和FSR 4上的合作早有先例，特别是在BVH优化方面。
• brcmthrowaway提出谁是更好的计算机架构师，Mark Cerny还是Anand Shimpi，引发对两位技术专家的比较。
• lofaszvanitt质疑，当前PS世代游戏数量有限，新技术应用的前景如何。
• shmerl询问Sony何时会在PS上支持Vulkan。
• ZenithExtreme提到，AMD的下一代GPU可能内含PlayStation技术。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及对Mark Cerny个人的高度评价，以及他在技术领域的贡献和影响力。
• 对AMD未来架构UDNA1的期待与担忧，特别是在软件支持和市场竞争方面的潜在风险。
• 对PlayStation技术路线的分析，包括RDNA和UDNA的演进以及具体技术（如FSR和BVH优化）的应用。
• 关于游戏主机与PC趋同的讨论，以及对未来游戏引擎和图形技术发展的看法。

data.title: Gene therapy restored hearing in deaf patients
data.author: justacrow
data.article_summary: 一项由瑞典卡罗林斯卡学院和中国多家医院及大学合作的新研究显示，基因疗法可以改善因OTOF基因突变导致的先天性耳聋或严重听力障碍患者的听力。研究对10名1至24岁的患者进行了治疗，使用合成腺相关病毒（AAV）将功能性OTOF基因注射到内耳。结果显示，所有患者在一个月内听力均有改善，六个月后平均可感知声音从106分贝降至52分贝。治疗安全且耐受良好，最常见的副作用是中性粒细胞减少。该研究为基因治疗耳聋开辟了新途径，未来有望应用于更多类型的遗传性耳聋。研究发表在《Nature Medicine》期刊上。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：基因疗法治疗耳聋的进展及其相关讨论

不同观点：
• [积极支持] jonathanlb 认为这是好消息，并希望这种疗法能扩展到其他形式的耳聋，如药物引起的耳毒性、耳部感染和一般的感音神经性听力损失。
• [相关趋势] vonnik 提到相邻领域的进展，引用了一个关于失明基因疗法的链接。
• [诊断问题] jhaddow 提问如何确定自己是否有这种类型的听力损失，特别是对于出生以来就有中度至重度听力损失的情况。
• [适应挑战] S4H 关注的是长期失聪的人在重新获得听力后可能面临的适应挑战。

补充讨论：
• [基因技术的推动力] max_ 提到当前许多进步是由遗传学推动的，并询问CRISPR/Cas9是否是这些进展的核心技术，同时质疑基因编辑股票表现不佳的原因。
• [对传统观念的冲击] Elaris 认为听力问题通常被认为难以治愈，但这种新研究可能改变许多过去被视为不可逆的状况，并对医学进步表示赞赏。
• [企业进展] smath 提到Regeneron在2025年2月公布了其基因疗法治疗耳聋的积极结果。
• [学术资源获取] FranckDernoncou 对研究论文在付费墙后表示不满，并提供了一个链接。
• [社区反应] d0100 希望了解聋人社区如何看待这类消息，并将其与对人工耳蜗植入的敌意进行比较。
• [伦理争议] squigz 提出在治疗自闭症时有类似的伦理讨论，质疑为什么有些被视为需要修正的残疾，而有些则被视为人类美丽的一部分。
• [历史对比] UltraSane 提到历史上脊椎按摩疗法声称治愈耳聋的例子，强调科学方法的重要性。
• [社区内部争议] froggertoaster 认为耳聋被一些社区视为存在和身份的威胁，并指出有些人认为耳聋是一种需要被治愈的残疾，而另一些人则持不同观点。
• [其他需求] coolKid721 则关注能否治愈耳鸣。

争议焦点：
1. 聋人社区对基因疗法治疗耳聋的不同看法，部分人可能认为这是对身份的威胁，而另一些人则希望获得治愈。
2. 在更广泛的医学伦理讨论中，类似治疗是否被视为修正残疾或接受多样性的选择。

Published: 02-07-2025 11:00 | Updated: 02-07-2025 11:11
Gene therapy restored hearing in deaf patients
Image:
Caption:
Photo: Getty Images
Gene therapy can improve hearing in children and adults with congenital deafness or severe hearing impairment, a new study involving researchers at Karolinska Institutet reports. Hearing improved in all ten patients, and the treatment was well-tolerated. The study was conducted in collaboration with hospitals and universities in China and is published in the journal Nature Medicine.
Image:
Caption:
Maoli Duan. Photo: Ulf Sirborn
“This is a huge step forward in the genetic treatment of deafness, one that can be life-changing for children and adults,” says
Maoli Duan
, consultant and docent at the
Department of Clinical Science, Intervention and Technology
, Karolinska Institutet, Sweden, and one of the study’s corresponding authors.
The study comprised ten patients between the ages of 1 and 24 at five hospitals in China, all of whom had a genetic form of deafness or severe hearing impairment caused by mutations in a gene called OTOF. These mutations cause a deficiency of the protein otoferlin, which plays a critical part in transmitting auditory signals from the ear to the brain.
Effect within a month
The gene therapy involved using a synthetic adeno-associated virus (AAV) to deliver a functional version of the OTOF gene to the inner ear via a single injection through a membrane at the base of the cochlea called the round window.
The effect of the gene therapy was rapid and the majority of the patients recovered some hearing after just one month. A six-month follow-up showed considerable hearing improvement in all participants, the average volume of perceptible sound improving from 106 decibels to 52.
The younger patients, especially those between the ages of five and eight, responded best to the treatment. One of the participants, a seven-year-old girl, quickly recovered almost all her hearing and was able to hold daily conversations with her mother four months afterwards. However, the therapy also proved effective in adults.
“Smaller studies in China have previously shown positive results in children, but this is the first time that the method has been tested in teenagers and adults, too,” says Dr Duan. “Hearing was greatly improved in many of the participants, which can have a profound effect on their life quality. We will now be following these patients to see how lasting the effect is.”
No serious adverse reactions
The results also show that the treatment was safe and well-tolerated. The most common adverse reaction was a reduction in the number of neutrophils, a type of white blood cell. No serious adverse reactions were reported in the follow-up period of 6 to 12 months.
“OTOF is just the beginning,” says Dr Duan. “We and other researchers are expanding our work to other, more common genes that cause deafness, such as GJB2 and TMC1. These are more complicated to treat, but animal studies have so far returned promising results. We are confident that patients with different kinds of genetic deafness will one day be able to receive treatment.”
The study was conducted in collaboration with a number of institutions, including Zhongda Hospital, Southeast University, China, and was financed by several Chinese research programmes and Otovia Therapeutics Inc., the company that has developed the gene therapy and that employs many of the researchers involved in the study. See the published paper for a full list of conflicts of interest.
Publication
”AAV gene therapy for autosomal recessive deafness 9: a single-arm trial”
, Jieyu Qi, Liyan Zhang, Ling Lu, Fangzhi Tan, Cheng Cheng, Yicheng Lu, WenXiu Dong, Yinyi Zhou, Xiaolong Fu, Lulu Jiang, Chang Tan, Shanzhong Zhang, Sijie Sun, Huaien Song, Maoli Duan, Dingjun Zha, Yu Sun, Xia Gao, Lei Xu, Fan-Gang Zeng, Renjie Chai,
Nature Medicine
, online 2 July 2025, doi: 10.1038/s41591-025-03773-w.

data.title: Escher's art and computer science
data.author: signa11
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了Gritzko的librdx项目。该项目在GitHub上公开可用，用户必须登录才能更改通知设置。目前，该项目有3个分支（Fork）和88个星标（Star）。文章简要说明了项目的公开状态和一些基础的互动数据，如分支和星标数量。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对Escher的艺术影响及个人经历的讨论

不同观点：
• [nativeit] 分享了自己在20多岁时纹上Escher自画像的个人经历，认为这是自己成长过程的一部分，没有后悔。他提到朋友的姐姐用稀释的黑墨水模拟铅笔画效果，成功呈现了Escher作品的质感。
• [bdamm] 对[nativeit]的评论进行了讽刺，认为其叙述像是一个未经历现实打击的“成长故事”，暗示软件开发者最终需要面对实际工作的压力和结果。
• [megaloblasto] 简单表达了对Escher艺术的喜爱，回忆自己小时候看到Escher的石版画感到震撼。
• [gritzko] 作为原文作者，对文章质量表示歉意，解释其写作是在一个短暂兴奋状态下快速完成的，没有经过仔细编辑。
• [kleiba] 批评原文的写作风格，认为其过于自负。
• [jochem9] 分享了一个关于Escher的轶事，指出Escher虽然不理解数学家的理论，但仍然享受他人对其作品的解读和赞赏。
• [awaymazdacx5] 以一句“试试用酒来理解这个”作为评论，似乎带有调侃或建议用放松的方式去理解Escher的作品。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点似乎在于[nativeit]的个人经历叙述被[bdamm]和[kleiba]认为是自负或不够成熟的表达。
• [jochem9]分享的Escher轶事提供了一个有趣的视角，即Escher本人对其作品的数学解读并不了解，但仍然乐见他人的解读。
• [gritzko]对原文质量的道歉表明作者意识到文章可能存在不足，但没有深入讨论。

data.title: A Higgs-Bugson in the Linux Kernel
data.author: Ne02ptzero
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了作者在Linux内核中遇到的一种难以重现的“Higgs-bugson”问题，影响了处理公司交易数据的系统（Gord）。问题表现为文件复制操作偶尔会失败，出现“权限被拒绝”（-EACCES）的错误，尽管文件权限设置正确。经过调查，作者怀疑问题与NFS和Kerberos认证相关。在NFS使用Kerberos时，内核通过`rpc_gssd`守护进程获取用户凭证，但检查日志未发现凭证问题。为重现问题，作者进行了多种测试，包括生成大文件和创建内存文件系统，最终通过一个内存内虚拟文件系统成功重现并理解了问题根源，涉及Kerberos凭证和NFS交互的复杂性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕"Higgs-Bugson"术语的讨论、NFS与Kerberos在系统中的使用问题、Linux内核质量的讨论以及对技术术语来源的考据。

不同观点：
• **Higgs-Bugson术语的合理性**：
   - **gnfargbl**：认为"Higgs-Bugson"这个术语不准确，因为Higgs粒子的发现困难源于其生产截面低、衰变特征难以分离等技术难题，而非不确定性或难以复现性。他将寻找Higgs粒子类比为在巨大玉米田中寻找特定类型的发光虫子，强调了技术挑战。

A Higgs-bugson in the Linux Kernel
Jul 02, 2025 |
13 min read
Share on Facebook
Share on Twitter
Share on LinkedIn
By:
Nikhil Jha
We recently ran across a strange higgs-bugson that manifested itself in a critical system that stores and distributes the firm’s trading activity data, called Gord. (A
higgs-bugson
is a bug that is reported in practice but difficult to reproduce, named for the
Higgs boson
, a particle which was theorized in the 1960s but only found in 2013.) In this post I’ll walk you through the process I took to debug it. I tried to write down relevant details as they came up, so see if you can guess what the bug is while reading along.
Some useful background information about NFS with Kerberos
The NFS (“Network File System”) protocol is designed to access a regular POSIX filesystem over the network. The default security story of NFSv3, which is what we’re using here, is roughly “no security” on an untrusted network: the server only checks whether or not the client is connected from a ”privileged” port number (i.e. less than 1024). If the client says it’s connecting on behalf of a particular user, the server just trusts the client. What could go wrong?
The other security option for NFS is Kerberos. When used with NFS, Kerberos cryptographically verifies the identity of the user accessing the file.
What’s the bug?
Gord often does large file copies to ship data around. These copies would very rarely fail with
-EACCES (Permission denied)
despite the permissions being correctly set on the filesystem. Although retries were possible, it would be sad to lose progress copying these files. Also, strange errors in data storage are scary! It’s possible that spurious errors could indicate a larger issue.
There was no obvious pattern in these copies failing. Even identical jobs running simultaneously didn’t necessarily fail together. We did have one clue: if we switched Kerberos off in the dev environment (because the error sounded auth related), the copies never failed.
So, maybe something was wrong with the Kerberos credentials?
How does the kernel get your Kerberos credentials?
In a typical userspace program making use of Kerberos, libkrb5 will parse some environment variables or a config file to find the location of a Kerberos credentials cache. However, applications using NFS don’t need to link libkrb5 or otherwise know anything about Kerberos. They just do normal file I/O syscalls (open, read, write, etc) as if they were accessing a local filesystem. So what’s going on?
It turns out the kernel gets credentials via a root userspace daemon called
rpc_gssd
. When your application does its first I/O syscall to a file on NFS, the kernel writes to a file on a special mountpoint to communicate with
rpc_gssd
. (Fun fact: this mountpoint,
rpc_pipefs
, is an entirely separate filesystem implementation in the Linux kernel, just like
ext4
or
nfs
itself.)
Making some simplifications, the rpc_gssd program grabs the user’s credentials, constructs the right Kerberos service ticket, and writes to the rpc_pipefs again with the result. This involves an API called GSSAPI (“Generic Security Services API”), which you’ll see mentioned throughout this post.
Looking at the rpc_gssd logs around the time of the bug, I noticed that the kernel hadn’t requested credentials for a while. The most recently requested credential should also have been fresh for another few hours. So, this was a dead end.
Trying to reproduce the bug
I decided to try my luck by running a slow trickle of writes over the weekend. It seemed like the issue would be key-related somehow, so having a long-running process would force key expiry and plausibly reproduce the bug.
Checking back in on Monday, none of the dozen boxes I ran this on failed. This wasn’t too surprising, because the issue was pretty rare in production.
I then generated some large (~200GB) random files, put them on a test NFS mount, and started copying them to another test NFS mount in a loop on even more boxes. Once again, none of these copies failed.
At this point I was surprised I hadn’t seen the issue. To make sure I wasn’t just getting extremely unlucky, I decided to scale up the number of copies running in parallel.
I was worried about wasting bandwidth and impacting other users, so I thought a bit about how to make the test a bit more lightweight. One easy win would be to copy from a local disk to NFS instead of from NFS to NFS. However, I had already requested boxes with tiny disks. Fortunately, I had a cool trick in mind.
Writing a filesystem
I decided to create a filesystem that contains large random files, but fits entirely in memory on small test machines. Here’s the idea: Instead of storing actual file content, I’d use a noise function (or hash function) to generate consistent random bytes on demand.
This turns out to be fairly straightforward. There’s a Rust crate called
fuser
that provides a nicely typed implementation of FUSE (“Filesystem in USErspace”). Around 20 minutes lat

TRANS-TAIGA ROAD
Detailed Travel Guide
Driving the Trans-Taiga Road
Overview Map
Virtual Tour
The Trans-Taiga Road is a gravel road that runs 666 km east
from near the top end of the
James Bay Road
. It
was built to access the various dams and generating stations that extend upriver
along the La Grande River.
This is an
extremely remote
road, leading 666 km
east - almost to Labrador - with no settlements or towns aside from Hydro
Quebec's settlements for workers (not open to the public). At the far end you
will be 745 km from the nearest town! This is the farthest you can get from a
town on a road in North America! (Not counting the private Hydro Quebec towns
that are not open to the public). Along this road is also the
farthest north
point you
can travel on a road in eastern Canada.
The road from
Brisay
(km 582)
to
Caniapiscau
is rougher and a 4-wheel
drive vehicle is recommended by Hydro Quebec. The main reason for this is the
very coarse gravel used for this road - there's large rocks littering the road
surface. However, I have heard from people who have driven this road in ordinary
passenger cars and they say it is fine. You do have to keep your eyes open for
the larger rocks though.
You should definitely travel this road only in a reliable
vehicle with good tires. It is not an overly rough road; passenger vehicles can
drive it, but it is gravel. Vehicle breakdowns here can be very costly. Flat
tires can be a serious (and expensive) incident if your tires are damaged. You
could be looking at having tires flown in on a non-scheduled flight - there are
no convenient "tire stores" up here! Please read
Driving the Trans-Taiga Road
first.
Although there are no towns, there are a couple of outfitters
along the way that sell fuel and offer meals and lodging. Cell phones do not
work here.
Generally the scenery is fairly level, but this road is
definitely more interesting than the
James Bay Road
. For
most of the length it runs through taiga: spruce and jack pine forest, bogs,
rocks, and low hills. This is about all you'll see apart from birds and some
wildlife, the occasional cabin a short distance off the road, and Hydro Quebec
installations. I once saw a couple of wolves playing in the middle of this road.
This truly is a
*VERY*
remote road. Do not approach a trip along it lightly.
Please read
Driving the Trans-Taiga Road
before traveling this road.

Conversations
with
a Hit Man
A former FBI agent traveled to Louisiana to ask a hired killer about a murder that haunted him. Then they started talking about a different case altogether.
By David Howard
The
Atavist
Magazine, No. 164
David Howard is a journalist and the author of
Chasing Phil: The Adventures of Two Undercover Agents with the World’s Most Charming Con Man
. He previously worked as an editor for
Backpacker
,
Bicycling
,
Popular Mechanics
,
and
Prevention
.
Editor:
Jonah Ogles
Art Director:
Ed Johnson
Copy Editor:
Sean Cooper
Fact Checker:
Kyla Jones
Illustrator:
Björn Griesbach
Published in June 2025.
1
The killer is happy
to see us. That’s the first thing we notice when we spot Larry Thompson halfway across the visitation room of the David Wade Correctional Center. He rises from a chair and waves, his face unfurling into an avuncular grin. Our separate journeys to this prison in Homer, Louisiana—me from Maine, and Myron Fuller from the mountains of Utah—afforded plenty of time to set expectations, and neither of us anticipated a Norman Rockwell greeting. I pictured a menacing scene bathed in the neo-noir lighting of
The Silence of the Lambs.
And Fuller? He long believed that the next time he and Thompson saw each other would be through gun sights.
The visitation room Warden Jerry Goodwin escorted us into is large, square, and filled with cafeteria-style tables. It’s December 2021. Lights on a small artificial Christmas tree wink, at once cheery and monstrously sad. Vending machines line one wall, glowing sentinels filled with bags of junk food. During normal visiting hours, the chatter of reunited families animates the room. But Fuller is a retired FBI agent with an illustrious career, I’m an experienced journalist, and Thompson is a model inmate, his vast criminal history notwithstanding. As such, Goodwin has granted us special privileges: an open-ended block of time, and a dedicated room with no bars or glass partitions, just a bored-looking guard at a nearby desk.
“Larry,” Fuller says.
“Good to see you,” Thompson drawls. The two old adversaries take chairs facing each other across six feet of wood laminate. I perch on a bench halfway between them and fan out the objects I’ve been permitted: notepad, pen, digital recorder.
At 78, Thompson is 18 years into an 80-year prison sentence for attempted first-degree murder and aggravated burglary. (A 35-year federal term theoretically begins after that.) One morning in 2003, Larry and his son Larry Neal Thompson Jr., along with four other men, robbed an Intertrust Armored Services car. They were spotted by a witness—a rare event in Thompson’s long criminal career—and a cop chased their escape van. One of the men shot an AK-47 through the officer’s window, wounding him. A massive manhunt ensued, and after several hours all six of the perpetrators were caught. They were subsequently convicted. Then, in 2014, Thompson confessed to four murders for hire in exchange for a reduced prison term for his son. (That deal never went through, because the official who overseeing it died before it could be finalized.) Thompson was later transferred to Wade from the maximum-security Louisiana State Penitentiary—better known as Angola.
Seated before us, he wears the standard-issue uniform: blue jeans and a light-blue chambray shirt. His hangdog blue eyes are framed by gaffer-taped tortoiseshell glasses that rest atop his prominent nose. His hands are missing parts of two fingers. “This one I cut off with an electric drill,” he’ll tell us later, holding up the stump of his left index finger. Then he’ll wave the remains of his right ring finger. “My dog bit me on this one.”
The warden tells us goodbye, then turns to Thompson. “Behave yourself,” he says, not unpleasantly. Goodwin hesitates for a beat, as if he wants to say something to us or is curious about why we’re here. Cops come to interview prisoners all the time, of course, but he doesn’t see many 79-year-old retired FBI agents dropping in on one of his more notorious inmates.
Fuller shakes Goodwin’s hand and thanks him. The truth, as best Fuller can grasp it himself, is that he’s hoping to dislodge a few ghosts from his psyche. He enjoyed an illustrious 31-year career in the bureau, with one notable exception: his tenure running the office in Shreveport, Louisiana, from 1981 to 1985.
What went wrong? Only everything. Crooked cops. Investigations that inexplicably faceplanted. Political interference. Wiseguys and one particularly ethically challenged attorney. And, most prominently, a murder Fuller believes he could have prevented: Maria Marshall, a mother of three. It was a hired job; her husband, saddled with debt, wanted to collect the life insurance. The hit man was Larry Thompson.

data.title: Nightmares Linked to Faster Ageing and Premature Mortality
data.author: gnabgib
data.article_summary: 新研究发现，频繁的噩梦与生物学上的加速衰老以及过早死亡风险增加三倍有关。英国痴呆症研究所的Abidemi Otaiku博士分析了4196名26至74岁成人的数据，结果显示，每周做噩梦的人过早死亡风险显著增加。研究通过表观遗传时钟测量生物衰老速度，发现频繁噩梦者衰老速度更快。噩梦通过加速细胞衰老过程，解释了约39%的噩梦与过早死亡之间的关系。因此，频繁噩梦应被视为加速衰老和早死的可修改风险因素，临床实践中应筛查并治疗噩梦，以改善睡眠质量、心理健康，并可能降低死亡风险。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：梦境与 nightmare（噩梦）的成因、变化以及可能的干预方法

不同观点：
• **lqet** 分享了自己在有孩子之前经常做关于杀人 guilt（罪恶感）的噩梦，但在第一个孩子出生后噩梦就停止了。这暗示了生活阶段的变化（如成为父母）可能对梦境有影响。
  
• **jkmcf** 表示自己长达45年一直做噩梦，且不认为这与缺乏锻炼或衰老有直接关系，似乎认为噩梦是长期存在且不可解释的现象。

• **BLKNSLVR** 提到自己很少做梦或记住梦，并认为对噩梦的了解可能反而会让人做更多噩梦。同时，他指出对现实的接受态度可能影响梦境记忆，但不确定这两者是否相关。

• **3shv** 以幽默方式表示自己多数梦到的是死亡，认为这可能预示着自己的未来，暗示梦境可能与个人对命运的看法有关。

• **NoPicklez** 提出了饮食（特别是乳制品）可能导致 GI distress（胃肠不适），从而引发噩梦的观点，并引用了相关文章，提出食物不耐受可能影响梦境质量。

• **rapjr9** 分享了个人经历，提到服用 NAD+ 补充剂（Elysium Health's Basis）后梦境变得无趣，暗示补充剂可能有减少噩梦的效果，尽管只是 anecdotal evidence（个人经验）。

• **billy99k** 观察到戒掉咖啡因后，梦境记忆恢复且睡眠质量改善，暗示咖啡因可能对梦境和睡眠有影响。

补充讨论：
• **争议的焦点**：梦境的成因尚无定论，不同人对于梦境的变化有不同的解释，包括心理因素（如生活阶段变化、对现实的态度）、生理因素（如饮食、补充剂）等。

• **饮食与梦境的关系**：NoPicklez 和 billy99k 提到了饮食（乳制品、咖啡因）对梦境和睡眠的影响，这为梦境的生理成因提供了可能的解释。

• **干预方法**：rapjr9 提到 NAD+ 补充剂可能对减少噩梦有效，尽管这是基于个人经验，但提供了一种潜在的干预思路。

• **梦境与现实的关系**：部分评论（如 BLKNSLVR 和 3shv）提到了梦境与现实态度、命运预示等的关系，反映了梦境可能具有的心理暗示作用。

44449958.article_content:
FREQUENT nightmares are linked to accelerated biological ageing and a threefold increase in the risk of premature death, according to new research presented at EAN 2025  by Dr Abidemi Otaiku of the UK Dementia Research Institute.
Nightmares have long been associated with neurodegenerative diseases, but their broader impact on health and ageing has remained unclear. This study is the first to demonstrate that nightmares are not only distressing but may also be a significant, independent predictor of faster biological ageing and earlier mortality in the general population.
The study analysed data from 4,196 adults aged 26 to 74, drawn from four large population-based cohort studies, with a total follow-up of 18 years. Nightmare frequency was self-reported at baseline, and premature mortality was defined as death before age 75. The study used Cox regression to examine the association between nightmare frequency and premature death, while biological ageing rates were measured using a composite of three epigenetic clocks (DunedinPACE, GrimAge, PhenoAge). During the follow-up period, 227 premature deaths occurred. Adults who reported weekly nightmares at baseline had a more than threefold increased risk of dying before 75 compared to those with no nightmares (adjusted hazard ratio 2.73; p<0.001). Furthermore, individuals with frequent nightmares exhibited significantly faster rates of biological ageing (p<0.001). Mediation analysis revealed that accelerated biological ageing explained approximately 39% of the relationship between nightmares and premature mortality, suggesting that the stress and sleep disruption caused by nightmares may directly impact cellular ageing processes.
These findings highlight the importance of recognising and addressing nightmares as a modifiable risk factor for accelerated ageing and early death. For clinical practice, this suggests that patients presenting with frequent nightmares should be screened for underlying sleep disorders, stress, and mental health issues, and offered appropriate interventions such as cognitive behavioural therapy for insomnia or image rehearsal therapy. Given that nightmares are both common and treatable, targeted interventions could not only improve sleep quality and mental well-being but may also contribute to healthier ageing and reduced mortality risk. Further research is needed to confirm whether treating nightmares can slow biological ageing and extend lifespan, but the evidence already supports a proactive approach to nightmare management in routine healthcare.
Reference
Otaiku A. Nightmares accelerate biological aging and predict premature mortality in humans. Abstract OPR-111. EAN Congress, 21-24 June, 2025.

data.title: Astronomers discover 3I/ATLAS – Third interstellar object to visit Solar System
data.author: gammarator
data.article_summary: MPEC 2025-N12报告了ATLAS望远镜发现的一个新天体：3I/ATLAS = C/2025 N1 (ATLAS)。该天体在四张于7月1日拍摄的图像中被发现，拥有高度偏心、超双曲轨道（e ~ 6）。初步观察显示可能有彗星活动，伴随微弱彗发和3角秒长的尾迹。观测数据来自多位天文学家，进一步的观测被鼓励以精确确定其轨道和性质。所有观测数据可通过MPC Explorer实时获取。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕新发现的第三个星际物体（3I）的科学分析、可能性推测以及未来观测的讨论。

不同观点：
• **科学分析与数据解读**：
  - [ddahlen] 提供专业见解，解释该星际物体的轨道特性（偏心率超过6）、大小估计（8-22公里，取决于表面反照率），并提到如果该物体活跃（如彗星），其尘埃可能使其看起来比实际大。他还指出该物体逆行，并预测其在接近太阳时的行为。
  - [jerpint] 则表示对数据不了解，询问如何将这些数据解释为一个实际物体。

• **天文观测技术的进步与未来发现**：
  - [ordu] 提出两种假设：人类天文学家观测技术的提升，或宇宙中即将出现大量类似物体。
  - [zeristor] 认为新投入使用的Vera Rubin望远镜将发现更多此类物体。
  - [jcfrei] 期待更大口径的望远镜（如ELT）上线，认为会带来更多新发现。

• **星际物体数量与宇宙学意义**：
  - [martinclayton] 引用了学术论文中的数据，讨论星际物体的数量估计，并进行计算推测在土星轨道范围内可能存在一个这样的物体。
  - [isx726552] 提到小说中的情节与现实中发现的对比，认为现实中发现的星际物体数量增加迅速。

• **对星际物体异常性质的讨论**：
  - [rjinman] 认为发现更多类似彗星的星际物体，使Oumuamua（1I）显得更加怪异。

• **科幻与假设**：
  - [fouronnes3] 提出科幻性假设，认为前两个星际物体是外星飞船的废弃阶段，而3I是主船。
  - [m3kw9] 表达希望该物体是外星智慧生命来访，尽管这是一个不受欢迎的观点。

• **人类应对与技术能力**：
  - [artur_makly] 询问如果该物体直接朝地球而来，人类目前是否有能力阻止。
  - [renrutal] 则开玩笑提到是否能搭便车，并指出只有Project Orion可能追上其速度。

补充讨论：
• **具体信息查询**：

data.title: You People Keep Contradicting Yourselves
data.author: taylorlunt
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了一种常见的网络争论现象：人们常常因为个人的言论与某个群体（或普遍观点）不一致，而指责其为伪善。文章以Bhavye Khetan欺骗风投获取会议的推文为例，分析了某人被指责为伪善，仅仅因为他与某个群体（即便与他本人无关）的言论相矛盾。作者指出，这种"关联伪善"的指责反映了社会的部落化倾向，人们更倾向于将个体视为群体的代表，而不是独立的个体。这种互动模式可能是有毒的，因为它忽视了个体的独特观点和独立性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：在线讨论中的假设、泛化、同理心以及社交媒体对话的质量

不同观点：
• danscan认为，人们常常会把个体当作某个群体的代言人来争论，并指责他人是伪君子，即使这些矛盾并非来自个体自身，而是来自群体中的其他人。这种现象让在线讨论变得令人疲惫。
• dataflow反驳danscan，认为他正在做自己所指责的行为，即错误地将言外之意归咎于他人。dataflow指出，Rob Bailey的评论并没有称任何人为伪君子，而是指出了一种常见的矛盾现象。dataflow还强调，人类自然会做出假设，这是正常的，解决方法是更合理地处理这些假设，并对他人观点抱有更多宽容。
• szszrk承认自己也会在争论中使用“总是”和“每个人”这样的泛化词语，并分享了自己试图通过设立规则来提高自我意识和同理心的努力。他还提出了是否应在压力下避免讨论以提高自我反省的问题。
• notarobot123指出，社交媒体的特性使得细微的讨论变得困难，例如广播消息需要某种程度的泛化、算法推荐扭曲了我们对共同背景的认知等。社交媒体的环境助长了部落主义，使得人们更容易将个体视为群体代表。
• briangriffinfan询问如何有效地指出他人的错误，而不会引发对方的下意识否认和反击，并质疑这种现象是否表明了讨论的恶意。
• scrubs认为，社交媒体激励极端立场和象征性的争斗，因为这可以带来关注和流量。这种环境使得人们更倾向于攻击群体而非个体。
• actuallyalys同情这种错误，认为部落主义部分解释了这种现象，但并不为其辩护。
• DonsDiscountGas质疑文章中的某个例子是否足以说明“游戏被操纵”。
• lijok认为，这种现象是由于人们的懒惰和寻找最廉价的方式来验证自己的世界观。
• moralestapia指责xir做了同样的错误行为，并提出一种讽刺性的解决方案。
• weare138批评Rob guy使用了稻草人论证和诉诸权威的经典诡辩技巧。
• subjectsigma表示，曾经试图分析这类问题，但后来意识到这种努力无助于改变现状，因此停止这样做。
• imtringued批评文章错失了一个解释推文回应中的问题的机会，而是使用了不相关的类比。
• love2read简单表示文章读起来不错。

补充讨论：
- 争议的焦点在于人们是否在在线讨论中容易做出错误的假设和泛化，以及如何有效地解决这种现象。
- 另一个值得注意的讨论点是社交媒体环境如何影响对话质量，特别是其对部落主义和极端立场的激励作用。
- 自我反省和同理心在在线讨论中的重要性也被多次提及，szszrk和dataflow都强调了理解和宽容的必要性。

44451313.article_content:
←
See all posts
You People Keep Contradicting Yourselves!
’politics’
’rationality’
I saw this tweet
1
recently:
A tweet by Bhavye Khetan in which he brags about tricking VCs into having mettings with him after he lied to them about his credentials
The guy lied to get meetings with VCs. As far as I can tell, this is the system operating exactly how it should, and I have really nothing to say about that. What I want to talk about is this popular response:
A response to Bhavye Khetan’s tweet by Rob Bailey, calling Bhavye Khetan a hypocrite.
Specifically, point #1. "People complain VCs don't take cold inbound. So don't complain if they try to."
Do you see the problem? Rob Bailey is calling Bhavye Khetan a hypocrite because Bhavye Khetan said something that contradicts something that "people" say. But "people" and Bhavye Khetan are not the same thing?
I'm not trying to pick on this Rob Bailey guy — it's a common pattern I've noticed online. People will argue with an individual as if that individual is the spokesperson for a larger group. People will call someone a hypocrite not for contradicting
themselves
, but for contradicting
other people
.
"Oh, you think sex work should be decriminalized? I was under the impression you feminists thought sex work was exploitative?"
Why should an individual feminist be beholden to what every other feminist has said? Maybe some feminists think sex work is exploitative and some don't. Yet too often people accuse others of
hypocrisy by association
. I bet now that I've pointed it out, you'll start seeing it everywhere.
2
If you say something that contradicts what a group you're loosely associated with has said (even if that group is just "people in general"), then you must be a hypocrite.
But why does this happen? Have we grown so tribalistic that our default mode of interaction is now team vs. team rather than person vs. person? Can we no longer recognize that individuals may have their own opinions that differ from those of their tribe? If so, that sounds pretty toxic. But maybe it's comforting to believe you're combatting an ideology, rather than a mess of millions of individuals who all have different lives and believe different things.
Footnotes
Actually, I saw
Anthony Sistilli's video about the tweet

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frequency_illusion

data.title: I scanned all of GitHub's "oops commits" for leaked secrets
data.author: elza_1111
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了AI编码助手可能带来的安全风险，并详细描述了如何利用GitHub Event API和GitHub Archive项目扫描所有"Oops Commits"以寻找泄露的秘密。作者Sharon Brizinov解释了即使在GitHub上强制推送删除提交，这些"悬空提交"仍然可以被访问。他与Truffle Security合作，开发了一个开源工具（Force Push Scanner）来扫描GitHub组织中隐藏的提交，从而发现价值25,000美元的漏洞奖励。文章还提供了如何使用简单脚本自动化这一过程的教程，强调了即使被删除的提交也可能会泄露敏感信息。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：如何处理GitHub上的"oops commits"（误提交的代码）以及如何有效管理敏感信息（如密钥）

不同观点：
• [Pwhy1] 认为通过活动标签可以看到所有提交，包括误提交的代码，但无法自行删除，必须联系支持团队。这令他感到困扰。
• [oefrha] 指出，虽然GitHub似乎永久保留悬空提交，但可以通过联系客服进行垃圾回收（garbage collect），并建议在误推送敏感信息后应立即进行密钥轮换和联系客服处理。
• [edverma2] 建议使用开源工具trufflehog作为预提交钩子来检测敏感信息，认为这是避免意外提交的有效方法，并对该方法未被广泛采用表示疑惑。
• [CHUCKZZZ] 推荐使用MailsAI来跟踪和管理敏感数据曝光，认为这可以简化处理提交的过程。
• [UnreachableCode] 质疑在私有库中出现误提交的问题，认为只要不是开源项目，这个问题的影响有限。
• [frollogaston] 提到Google AppEngine曾鼓励将密钥存储在YAML文件中，这容易导致误提交，且没有像Heroku那样简单的方法来管理密钥。
• [bob1029] 分享了自己使用环境变量的经验，认为这是避免误提交的有效方法，但也承认在Windows系统上配置环境变量较为麻烦。
• [ggm] 建议引入默认的安全删除选项，并讨论了如何在保留日志的同时清理历史记录。
• [Prickle] 自述在紧急情况下硬编码密钥的经历，强调在演示后立即轮换了密钥。

• [raesene9] 担心有人会实时检测并利用这些误提交的密钥，并认为未联系到的开发者可能仍然面临风险。

• 争议的焦点在于如何有效管理和删除误提交的敏感信息，尤其是在私有库和开源项目中的不同处理方式。

Guest Post: How I Scanned all of GitHubâs âOops Commitsâ for Leaked Secrets
Guest Post: How I Scanned all of GitHubâs âOops Commitsâ for Leaked Secrets
Sharon Brizinov
TL;DR
GitHub Archive logs every public commit, even the ones developers try to delete. Force pushes often cover up mistakes like leaked credentials by rewriting Git history. GitHub keeps these dangling commits, from what we can tell, forever. In the archive, they show up as âzero-commitâ
PushEvents
.
I scanned every force push event since 2020 and uncovered secrets worth
$25k in bug bounties
.
Together with Truffle Security, we're open sourcing a new tool to scan your own GitHub organization for these hidden commits (
try it here
).
The new open-source
Force Push Scanner
tool identifies secrets in dangling commits.
This guest post by Sharon Brizinov, a white-hat hacker, was developed through
Truffle Securityâs Research CFP program
. We first connected with Sharon after his widely shared write-up,
How I Made 64k From Deleted Files
, where he used TruffleHog to uncover high-value secrets in public GitHub repositories. In this follow-up, Sharon expanded his research to access 100% of deleted commits on GitHub. He takes a deeper dive into one of our favorite areas: secrets hidden in deleted GitHub commits.
Overview
What Does it Mean to Delete a Commit?
Github Event API
Finding all Deleted Commits
Building the Automation
Hunting for Impactful Secrets
Case Study - Preventing a Massive Supply-Chain Compromise
Summary
Background
My name is
Sharon Brizinov
, and while I usually focus on low-level vulnerability and exploitation research in OT/IoT devices, I occasionally dive into bug bounty hunting.
I recently published a
blog post
about uncovering secrets hidden in dangling blobs within GitHub repositories, which sparked quite a lively discussion. After the post, I had several conversations with various people including Dylan, the CEO of Truffle Security, who gave me some intriguing ideas for continuing to explore new methods for large-scale secret hunting. I decided to create a mind map with everything I know related to this topic and try to come up with a new idea.
Iâll spare you my messy sketch, but hereâs a roundup of the projects, blogs, ideas, and resources I zeroed in on (highly recommended):
Github Event API
Hidden GitHub Commits and How to Reveal Them by Neodyme.io
Anyone can Access Deleted and Private Repository Data on GitHub by TruffleHog
TruffleHog now finds all Deleted & Private Commits on GitHub by TruffleHog
TruffleHog Scans Deleted Git Branches by TruffleHog
Phantom Secrets: Undetected Secrets Expose Major Corporations by Aqua Security
gharchive
Eventually, I came up with a simple idea - I will use the Github Event API alongside the
GitHub Archive
project to scan all Zero-Commit Push-Events (deleted commits) for secrets. Everything was known, I just glued it together and built automation at scale that hunted for secrets.
In this blog, I will describe my journey from understanding why you can never really delete a commit in GitHub to how to find all of them and build automation around it.
What Does it Mean to Delete a Commit?
In my previous
blog post
, I discussed how I discovered supposedly deleted files within GitHub repositories. Specifically, I was able to reconstruct dangling blobs - objects that had been deleted and were no longer referenced by any commit or treeâ¦ Or so I thought. After chatting with the Truffle folks, it turns out these orphaned blobs actually had orphaned commits that went along with them. And with a little research, I was able to uncover 100% of those orphaned commits at scale, across all of GitHub.
Suppose youâve accidentally committed and pushed a secret to your repository. Whatâs the next step? Typically, youâd want to reset the HEAD to the previous commit and force-push the changes, effectively removing the current commit and making it unreferenced - essentially deleting it. Hereâs how you do it:
But as
neodyme
and
TruffleHog
discovered, even when a commit is deleted from a repository, GitHub never forgets. If you know the full commit hash, you can access the supposedly deleted content. Moreover, you don't even need the full commit has, as TruffleHog
discovered
- it's enough to brute-force just the first four hex-digits.
Force Pushing: A Tutorial
Letâs see this in action using my own repository:
test-oops-commit
. Try to locate the deleted commit -
9eedfa00983b7269a75d76ec5e008565c2eff2ef
.
To help visualize our commits, I prepared a simple bash script that shows the
commit-tree-blob
objects,
get_commits.sh
:
git
rev
-
list
--
all
|
while
read
commit
;
do
echo
"Commit: $commit"
git
cat
-
file
-
p
"$commit"
|
grep
'^tree\|^

data.article_summary: CoMaps是一款由社区驱动的开源导航应用，已在Google Play Store、Apple App Store和F-Droid发布。它支持离线搜索和路线规划，节省电池，且注重隐私保护，不识别用户、不追踪、不收集数据。该应用完全免费且无广告，所有开发决策公开透明，用户可以参与应用的 evolution。CoMaps专注于为社区创造价值，而非盈利。立即下载，探索您的旅程！
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：CoMaps（Organic Maps的一个社区主导的分支）的未来发展、治理模式、技术改进以及与类似应用的区别。

不同观点：
• **治理与所有权问题：**
  ◦ milliams担心CoMaps可能会重蹈其他分支的覆辙，出现所有权混乱或争议，建议建立中立的基金会或采用治理模式以避免这些问题。他提到不希望再次经历不断让亲友安装新分支的情况。
  
• **技术功能与性能：**
  ◦ jeroenhd认为OsmAnd功能丰富但可能对普通用户过于复杂，而Maps.me的分支（如CoMaps）虽然性能不错但功能有限，特别是在路径规划方面存在不足。他希望两个应用能和平共存并共同进步。
  ◦ eisa01指出CoMaps相较于Organic Maps在技术上做出了一些改进，如修复了iOS系统上的多个bug，包括CarPlay界面问题和路径显示问题。
  
• **兼容性问题：**
  ◦ phkahler提到当前一些OSM应用在Android Auto上的兼容性问题，希望CoMaps能解决这些使用上的不便。
  
• **地区特定问题：**
  ◦ spacemule指出在以色列，很多道路是禁止普通车辆通行的，而当前的导航应用（包括可能的CoMaps）没有像Waze那样避免这些道路，这使得他在使用上受限。
  
• **用户体验问题：**
  ◦ izacus对Organic Maps的导航体验提出批评，尤其是导航标记的抖动问题，认为缺乏运动滤镜和动量计算导致导航不准确且容易让用户错过转弯。他希望CoMaps能解决这一问题。

  ◦ teeray认为导航应用领域近年来缺乏创新，对CoMaps的进入表示欢迎，期待看到新的发展。
  
补充讨论：

  ◦ 多位用户（如worldsavior、jamil7、fluder）对CoMaps与Organic Maps的具体区别表示疑问，并询问为何要进行分支。

data.title: About AI Evals
data.author: TheIronYuppie
data.article_summary:
这篇文章总结了在教授700多名工程师和产品经理过程中遇到的常见问题，并提供了对AI评估（AI Evals）中一些关键问题的见解。文章主要内容包括：

1. **RAG是否已过时**：文章澄清了一个误解，即“RAG已死”仅针对某些特定应用（如编码代理）的简单向量数据库检索方式，而RAG（检索增强生成）作为一个整体概念仍然有效。开发者应根据具体应用选择合适的检索策略，而不是完全放弃检索。

2. **是否可以使用同一模型进行主要任务和评估**：通常可以使用同一模型家族作为评估 judge，但需确保其执行的是不同任务，并通过二元分类来提高真阳性率和真阴性率。不建议在开放式偏好或响应质量评估中使用同一模型。

3. **模型选择的时间投入**：不应一开始就专注于模型选择，而应通过错误分析了解系统的失败模式，再决定是否需要更换模型。

4. **自定义注释工具的必要性**：文章建议构建自定义注释工具，以显著提高工作流效率，并列举了自定义工具的诸多优势，如集成多系统上下文、根据具体产品需求渲染数据等。

最后，文章还提到他们将最后一次开设AI Evals课程，并提供了一个35%的折扣码。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI评估（AI Evals）的工具、方法和实践

不同观点：
• **支持使用开源工具**：[calebkaiser] 认为应从免费/开源平台开始，如Opik，因为该领域的工具在过去一年中有了很大进步，且这些工具比以往更好用。相比之下，[ReDeiPirati] 强烈反对建议重新发明轮子，推荐使用现有的开源软件如Label Studio，而不是从零构建。
• **对模型选择的看法不同**：[afro88] 不同意原文中关于先进行错误分析再考虑模型切换的建议，认为如果有明显的模型性能提升（如Gemini 2到2.5），直接使用最佳模型是合理的。而原文建议首先进行错误分析，而不是一开始就关注模型切换。
• **对自定义工具的需求存在争议**：[davedx] 对“自定义注释工具”的具体用途表示困惑，而[pamelafox] 则补充了大量关于评估指标、方法、基础设施和用户反馈的具体问题和实践经验，展示了自定义工具的多样化需求。
• **自动化评估工具的必要性**：[_jonas] 提出评估团队应专注于高信号响应的审查，并介绍了一种自动筛选不可信LLM响应的工具。这表明了对自动化工具帮助提高评估效率的需求。
• **对AI评估理论的怀疑**：[satisfice] 对AI评估实践的有效性表示怀疑，认为这些建议大多基于未经证实的经验，且AI测试AI的理论存在局限性，无法全面评估AI的漏洞。

补充讨论：
• **对“Hamel式”评估助手的期望**：[dbish] 希望有一个“Hamel in a box”式的评估助手，能够自动指导和改进其他AI代理的评估过程，反映了行业对自动化评估解决方案的渴望。
• **对AI评估基础概念的需求**：[andybak] 提到对“AI Eval”具体定义的需求，表明新手对该领域基础概念的理解尚不清晰，需要更多解释性内容。
• **对模型供应商一致性和可追溯性的关注**：[th0ma5] 强调了模型供应商的一致性和可追溯性问题，认为应有工具来监控和验证供应商的模型变更，以确保评估的可靠性。

This post curates the most common questions Shreya and I have recieved from
teaching 700+
engineers & PMs in AI Evals.
Warning: These are sharp opinions about what works in most cases. They are not universal truths. Use your judgment.
👉
We are teaching our last and final cohort of our
AI Evals course
next month
(we have to get back to building). Here is a
35% discount code
for readers of this post.
👈
Q: Is RAG dead?
Question: Should I avoid using RAG for my AI application after reading that
“RAG is dead”
for coding agents?
Many developers are confused about when and how to use RAG after reading articles claiming “RAG is dead.” Understanding what RAG actually means versus the narrow marketing definitions will help you make better architectural decisions for your AI applications.
The viral article claiming RAG is dead specifically argues against using
naive vector database retrieval
for autonomous coding agents, not RAG as a whole. This is a crucial distinction that many developers miss due to misleading marketing.
RAG simply means Retrieval-Augmented Generation - using retrieval to provide relevant context that improves your model’s output. The core principle remains essential: your LLM needs the right context to generate accurate answers. The question isn’t whether to use retrieval, but how to retrieve effectively.
For coding applications, naive vector similarity search often fails because code relationships are complex and contextual. Instead of abandoning retrieval entirely, modern coding assistants like Claude Code
still uses retrieval
—they just employ agentic search instead of relying solely on vector databases.similar to how human developers work.
You have multiple retrieval strategies available, ranging from simple keyword matching to embedding similarity to LLM-powered relevance filtering. The optimal approach depends on your specific use case, data characteristics, and performance requirements. Many production systems combine multiple strategies or use multi-hop retrieval guided by LLM agents.
Unforunately, “RAG” has become a buzzword with no shared definition. Some people use it to mean any retrieval system, others restrict it to vector databases. Focus on the fundamental goal: getting your LLM the context it needs to succeed. Whether that’s through vector search, agentic exploration, or hybrid approaches is a product and engineering decision that requires understanding your users’ failure modes and usage patterns.
Rather than following categorical advice to avoid or embrace RAG, experiment with different retrieval approaches and measure what works best for your application.
Q: Can I use the same model for both the main task and evaluation?
For LLM-as-Judge selection, using the same model is usually fine because the judge is doing a different task than your main LLM pipeline. The judges we recommend building do
scoped binary classification tasks
. Focus on achieving high True Positive Rate (TPR) and True Negative Rate (TNR) with your judge on a held out labeled test set rather than avoiding the same model family. You can use these metrics on the test set to understand how well your judge is doing.
When selecting judge models, start with the most capable models available to establish strong alignment with human judgments. You can optimize for cost later once you’ve established reliable evaluation criteria. We do not recommend using the same model for open ended preferences or response quality (but we don’t recommend building judges this way in the first place!).
Q: How much time should I spend on model selection?
Many developers fixate on model selection as the primary way to improve their LLM applications. Start with error analysis to understand your failure modes before considering model switching. As Hamel noted in office hours, “I suggest not thinking of switching model as the main axes of how to improve your system off the bat without evidence. Does error analysis suggest that your model is the problem?”
Q: Should I build a custom annotation tool or use something off-the-shelf?
Build a custom annotation tool.
This is the single most impactful investment you can make for your AI evaluation workflow. With AI-assisted development tools like Cursor or Lovable, you can build a tailored interface in hours. I often find that teams with custom annotation tools iterate ~10x faster.
Custom tools excel because:
They show all your context from multiple systems in one place
They can render your data in a product specific way (images, widgets, markdown, buttons, etc.)
They’re designed for your specific workflow (custom filters, sorting, progress bars, etc.)
Off-the-shelf tools may be justified when you need to coordinate dozens of distributed annotators with enterprise access controls. Even then, many teams find the configuration overhead and limitations aren’t worth it.

data.article_summary:
本文讨论了JavaScript中普通函数和箭头函数的区别。普通函数有三种创建方式：函数声明、函数表达式（可以是匿名或命名函数表达式）和箭头函数。

1. **函数声明**：如`function isVowel(chr) {}`，会被JavaScript引擎提升（hoisted），在整个作用域内可用。
2. **函数表达式**：如`const takeWhile = function ...`，可以是匿名或命名函数，但命名函数的名称不会绑定到作用域，仅在错误追踪时有用。
3. **箭头函数**：如`const dropWhile = (predicate, arr) => {...}`，总是匿名且为表达式，不能直接命名，但可以被引擎推断名称。

箭头函数简洁，但与普通函数不同，没有自己的`this`、`arguments`对象，也不能用作构造函数。选择哪种函数语法取决于具体需求和上下文。

Title:
Alice's Adventures in a Differentiable Wonderland -- Volume I, A Tour of the Land
Authors:
Simone Scardapane
View a PDF of the paper titled Alice's Adventures in a Differentiable Wonderland -- Volume I, A Tour of the Land, by Simone Scardapane
View PDF
Abstract:
Neural networks surround us, in the form of large language models, speech transcription systems, molecular discovery algorithms, robotics, and much more. Stripped of anything else, neural networks are compositions of differentiable primitives, and studying them means learning how to program and how to interact with these models, a particular example of what is called differentiable programming.
This primer is an introduction to this fascinating field imagined for someone, like Alice, who has just ventured into this strange differentiable wonderland. I overview the basics of optimizing a function via automatic differentiation, and a selection of the most common designs for handling sequences, graphs, texts, and audios. The focus is on a intuitive, self-contained introduction to the most important design techniques, including convolutional, attentional, and recurrent blocks, hoping to bridge the gap between theory and code (PyTorch and JAX) and leaving the reader capable of understanding some of the most advanced models out there, such as large language models (LLMs) and multimodal architectures.

data.article_summary: HomeBrew HN 是一个由 Leo、Lewis 和 Steffan 在伦敦开发的平台。用户可以通过点击 "Get Recommendations" 获取个性化的 Hacker News (HN) 帖子推荐。此外，用户还可以刷新帖子列表和编辑个人资料。该平台旨在提升 Hacker News 内容浏览的个性化和便捷性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：个人兴趣档案生成工具的评价与改进建议

不同观点：
• 支持与赞赏：  
  - gwintrob和drakonka对工具的整体设计表示赞赏，尤其是将个人档案以Markdown形式展示，并认为此工具很有创意和实用性。
  - huem0n认为该工具的界面设计（如颜色和UI）合理，且对于初步原型表示肯定，期待其持续学习和改进。
  - bstsb对工具从少量数据中准确总结个人兴趣表示惊讶，并对生成的个人档案感到满意。

• 对工具改进的建议：  
  - huem0n和mdrzn建议工具应结合用户的点赞和评论历史来生成更准确的兴趣档案。
  - pxc指出，对于小众兴趣用户，当前基于近期热门文章的采样方法不够有效，建议用户可以手动输入兴趣关键词以提高准确性，并建议工具分析文章内容而不仅是标题。
  - password4321提出，用户的点赞历史和评论可以作为公开信号用于改进推荐。

• 对推荐准确性的反馈：  
  - NitpickLawyer认为工具对他的技术兴趣分析相当准确，但希望可以与自己评论过的主题进行对比。
  - pxc则指出工具对他的兴趣分析有误，特别是在低层次技术细节和理论计算机科学方面的兴趣评估不准确。

• 其他功能与技术讨论：  
  - peterm4希望工具能整合对HN评论的兴趣分析，而不仅是文章本身。
  - mebazaa询问是否考虑过使用传统的推荐系统，并结合LLM生成合成偏好。
  - wasabi991011对如何评估文章（基于标题还是内容）提出疑问。
  - flexagoon幽默地表示自己的兴趣其实只与有趣的标题有关，而非文章内容。
  - simongray则感慨HN平台上LLM内容的泛滥。

补充讨论：
• wickedsight对工具的技术架构感兴趣，并希望了解更多技术细节，表明该工具在技术社区引起了专业兴趣。
• 整体上，评论中有多个用户对工具的个性化和持续学习能力提出了期望，并提供了具体改进建议。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对斯蒂芬·马拉美诗歌《骰子一掷永远取消不了偶然》中核心思想的解读及其应用

不同观点：
• Dropbysometime认为该诗歌表达了“偶然性无法被消除”的观点。他解释道，即使在艺术创作或人生历程中，偶然性可以作为一种催化剂或灵感来源，但其本质是无法被控制或消除的。他引用了诗歌中的“掷骰子”作为代表偶然和不可预测性的象征，并提到诗歌试图捕捉绝对性但失败了，反映了人类在控制偶然性方面的无力。他还指出，这首诗因其创新的排版和思想成为现代主义诗歌的奠基之作，强调了人类控制的局限性和偶然性的力量。最后，他以幽默的方式提到程序员对待生活和偶然性的态度。

• VinLucero从另一个角度出发，认为这首诗体现了智慧高于智力的价值，以及在任何时候成为通才而非专才的重要性。这一观点将诗歌的思想引申到了个人发展和生活哲学的层面，强调了广泛涉猎和灵活应对偶然性的重要性。

补充讨论：
• Dropbysometime提出了一个实际问题，即在偶然性（如运气好坏）对人生路径有重要影响的情况下，如何过上幸福生活（路径依赖问题）。这引发了对如何在不可控因素影响下寻求幸福和满足的思考。

• 两个评论者都对诗歌的艺术价值和思想深度表示赞赏，但他们的关注点不同：一个关注偶然性和控制的问题，另一个则强调智慧和通才的价值观。

• Dropbysometime以现代HTML作比喻，说明了诗歌的视觉和结构创新，这为理解诗歌的现代性和实验性提供了一个有趣的视角。

data.title: Locality of Behaviour (2020)
data.author: jstanley
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了**行为局部性（LoB）**原则，强调代码单元的行为应尽可能直观，以便于理解和维护。作者引用Richard Gabriel的观点，指出良好的代码应让程序员通过查看少量代码即可理解其行为。文章对比了使用htmx和jQuery实现AJAX请求的例子，前者行为明显直观，符合LoB原则，而后者行为分散，不易理解。LoB与**DRY（不重复自己）**和**SoC（关注点分离）**等其他原则可能产生冲突，开发者需根据具体情况做出权衡。总体而言，遵循LoB原则有助于提高软件的可维护性、质量和可持续性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：前端开发中的行为局部性、框架选择、CSS与JS的分离与组织方式、以及开发原则（如DRY、SoC）的应用。

不同观点：
• Swizec认为React等框架提供了行为的局部性，使代码更直观、易于理解，尽管HTMX也有其优点。他强调，无论是HTMX还是React，有经验的开发者都能写出好代码，而无经验的开发者则可能写出不好的代码。

• Qoez指出，React打破了关注点分离（SoC）的传统原则，但仍然被广泛采用。他对这种灵活性持保留态度，认为这些原则被“弯曲”了。

• Alganet认为，分离的CSS和JS不一定打破行为局部性，关键在于设计出分层的CSS和JS，而不是特定的样式。他强调需要接受一些设计上的限制，并给出具体的代码示例来说明好的和不好的实践。

• Jonathan-adly分享了早期使用hyperscript进行Server Sent Events编码的愉快经历，强调了这种方法提供的局部行为和有趣的编码体验。

• Incorrecthorse对不良ID命名（如`d1`）进行了简短的批评，认为这是不恰当的例子。

• Hobozilla提到AI和上下文工程，指出DRY和SoC原则可能会影响代理获取上下文的效率，并以垂直切片架构为例说明将所有层次集中在小范围内的好处。

• Shelajev认为“远距离的诡异行为”虽然听起来不好，但在遵循约定优于配置原则的框架中是常见的，例如在SpringBoot中添加依赖会自动生成新的端点和配置。

• Khy指出，好的抽象（如`hx-get="/clicked"`）会让人感觉行为是局部的，而糟糕的抽象（如`id="d1"`）则会让人感觉行为是诡异的远距离作用。

• Pier25认为样式是标记行为的一部分，虽然不涉及交互行为，但确实影响渲染行为。

• Ribs希望看到“模块化”这个词被更多地提及。

• BeetleB批评文章误解了DRY原则，认为DRY不仅仅是避免代码重复，还有更深层次的含义。

补充讨论：
- 讨论中多次提到行为的局部性与全局性问题，尤其是在不同框架和编码实践中的体现。
- 开发原则如DRY（不要重复自己）和SoC（关注点分离）在实际应用中的灵活性和限制被多次提及。
- 不同开发者对如何组织CSS和JS代码（如特定 vs. 分层样式规则）有不同看法，反映了实践中对设计自由度和可维护性的权衡。
- 对框架和编码实践的具体例子（如React、HTMX、hyperscript）的讨论，展示了不同开发者对工具和方法的偏好和批评。

Locality of Behaviour (LoB)
Carson Gross
May 29, 2020
“The primary feature for easy maintenance is locality: Locality is that characteristic of source code that enables a
programmer to understand that source by looking at only a small portion of it.” –
Richard Gabriel
The LoB Principle
Locality of Behaviour is the principle that:
The behaviour of a unit of code should be as obvious as possible by looking only at that unit of code
Discussion
The LoB principle is a simple prescriptive formulation of the quoted statement from
Richard Gabriel
.
In as much as it is possible, and in balance with other concerns, developers should strive to make the behaviour of
a code element obvious on inspection.
Consider two different implementations of an AJAX request in HTML, the first in
htmx
:
<
button
hx-get
=
"/clicked"
>Click Me</
button
>
and the second in
jQuery
:
$
(
"#d1"
).
on
(
"click"
,
function
(){
$
.
ajax
({
/* AJAX options... */
});
});
<
button
id
=
"d1"
>Click Me</
button
>
In the former, the behaviour of the
button
element is obvious on inspection, satisfying the LoB principle.
In the latter, the behaviour of the
button
element is spread out amongst multiple files.  It is difficult to know
exactly what the button does without a total knowledge of the code base.  This “spooky action at a distance” is a source
of maintenance issues and stands in the way of developers understanding of the code base.
The htmx example demonstrates good Locality of Behaviour, while the jQuery example has poor Locality of Behaviour.
Surfacing Behaviour vs. Inlining Implementation
A common objection to Locality of Behaviour is that it is inlining implementation details within a code unit, making the
code unit less abstract and more brittle.  However, it is important to make the distinction between inlining the
implementation
of some behaviour and inlining the invocation (or declaration) of some behaviour.
Consider functions in most programming languages: there is a distinction between the declaration of function and its
use at call sites.  A good function abstracts away its implementation details, but is also invoked in an obvious manner,
without any spooky action at a distance.
Increasing the obviousness of the behaviour of an element is, ceteris paribus, a good thing, but it falls to both end-developers
and especially framework developers to make LoB both as easy and as conceptually clean as possible.
Conflict With Other Development Principles
The LoB will often conflict with other software development principles.  Two important ones
are:
DRY - Don’t Repeat Yourself
Software developers typically strive to avoid redundancy in their code or data.  This has come to be called “Staying DRY”,
i.e. Don’t Repeat Yourself.  Like other software design principles this, on its own, is a good thing.  htmx, for example,
allows you to place many attributes on parent elements in a DOM and avoid repeating these attributes on children.  This is a
violation of LoB, in favor of DRY, and such tradeoffs need to be made judiciously by developers.
Note that the further behaviour gets from the code unit it effects, the more severe the violation of LoB.  If it is
within a few lines of the code unit, this is less serious than if it is a page away, which is less serious than if
it is in a separate file entirely.
There is no hard and fast rule, but rather subjective tradeoffs that must be made as software developers.
SoC - Separation Of Concerns
Separation of concerns a design principle for separating a computer program into distinct sections such that each
section addresses a separate concern.  A canonical example of this is splitting HTML, CSS, and Javascript.  Again, on its own and
in isolation this may, indeed, be a good thing.  Inlining styles
has become more prevalent lately
,
but there are still strong arguments in favor of SoC in this regard.
Note that SoC is, however, in conflict with LoB.  By tweaking a CSS file the look and, to an extent, behaviour of an
element can change dramatically, and it is not obvious where this dramatic change came from.  Tools can help to an extent
here, but there is still “spooky action at a distance” going on.
Again, this isn’t to condemn SoC wholesale, just to say that there are subjective tradeoffs that must be made when
considering how to structure your code.  The fact that inline styles have become more prevalent as of late is an
indication that SoC is losing some support amongst developers.
Conclusion
LoB is a subjective software design principle that can help make a code base more humane and maintainable.  It must be traded
off against other design principles and be considered in terms of the limitations of the system a code unit is
written in, but, as much as is it is practical, adherence to this principle will increase your software maintainability,
quality and sustainability.

data.title: Doom Didn't Kill the Amiga (2024)
data.author: blakespot
data.article_summary: 文章讲述了作者作为Amiga电脑的忠实用户，回顾了Amiga的兴衰历程。作者在1988年首次接触Amiga 500，并于1992年购买了一台Amiga 500+。在当时，Amiga以其优越的图形和声音表现超越了其他家用电脑，如C64和Atari ST。尽管PC开始崭露头角，但在1992年，Amiga在性价比和游戏体验上仍具优势。然而，随着技术迅速发展，PC硬件价格下降，尤其是像《Doom》这样的游戏出现，使得PC逐渐成为强劲对手。虽然有人认为《Doom》导致了Amiga的衰落，但作者认为这只是技术发展的一个表现，而非根本原因。Commodore在硬件更新上的频繁变动和未能跟上技术潮流才是Amiga衰落的主因。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Amiga电脑的衰落原因及不同用户视角

不同观点：
• **个人经历视角：Amiga因游戏迁移到PC**  
  [runjake] 提到自己在1992年因为《Wolfenstein 3D》游戏从Amiga转向PC，并指出大多数朋友也已经转向其他平台。他还提到《Doom》在1993年发布，进一步加速了这一转变。

• **游戏机竞争视角：游戏机淘汰了Amiga**  
  [louthy] 认为游戏机（如家用游戏机）的兴起淘汰了Amiga等以游戏为主的家庭电脑，而PC因为用于商业用途得以幸存。他指出自己不认识任何用Amiga做非游戏用途的人。

• **地域差异视角：英国80-90年代电脑普及情况**  
  [bhlkjlkjcd] 对[louthy]的观点提出异议，基于自己在英国的经历指出，20世纪80年代末到90年代初，英国的孩子们普遍拥有各种8位和16位电脑，而非游戏机。他提到自己所在的社区大多数孩子拥有Commodore 64、Sinclair Spectrum等电脑，而非游戏机。

• **PC游戏优势视角：PC的崛起与Amiga的局限**  
  [leshokunin] 作为长期PC玩家，认为1993-1996年是PC游戏市场的巅峰期，列举了多款当时流行的PC游戏如《Day of the Tentacle》、《Myst》等，并提到PC游戏在技术和内容上的领先，使得Amiga显得不再必要。

• **Amiga的特定用途存续：专业应用延缓其消亡**  
  [mzs] 提到Amiga因特定应用（如Video Toaster）在某些领域存续了一段时间，甚至到2001年还有电视台使用Amiga系统。

• **技术局限视角：Amiga技术架构的过时**  
  [cmrdporcupine] 从技术角度分析Amiga的衰落，指出其芯片设计和内存行为导致其无法跟上技术发展，尤其是当内存和总线速度大幅提升时。他还提到Atari ST的用户体验，并认为转向486和Linux是更合理的选择。

• **Amiga产品定位争议：是否应作为游戏机推出**  
  [andrewstuart] 认为Amiga本质上是作为游戏机伪装成电脑，并提出如果Amiga一开始就作为CD32这种游戏机推出，或许公司还能存活至今。

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点：Doom是否导致Amiga的衰落**  
  [ChrisArchitect] 分享了一个视频链接，认为《Wolfenstein 3D》而非《Doom》才是Amiga衰落的原因，并引发进一步讨论。

总体来看，讨论围绕Amiga电脑的衰落原因展开，涉及个人经历、地域差异、技术局限以及Amiga的产品定位等多方面因素。

how doom didn't kill the amiga
How Doom didn't kill the Amiga
A detailed account of the rise and fall of an Amiga zealot
Early 2024
A scene from the Amiga game Defender of the Crown, released in 1986.
For years, no other home computer came close to screens like these.
Ever since I saw an Amiga 500 at a friend's house in what was probably late 1988, I wanted one for myself. Back then, computers were uncommon, especially at home. Even though I went to a school in a fairly affluent neighborhood, few kids had home computers or video games.
Gradually, that started to change.
I bought my own Amiga in February 1992. It was basically the same exact model as the one I had first seen in 1988: An Amiga 500+ with a 7 MHz 68000 CPU, 1 meg of RAM, 8-bit stereo PCM sound and many various graphics modes, of which 320x256 in 16 or 32 colors was the most common for games.
Competing Platforms
Buying any other computer was completely out of the question. There were practical reasons of course: I knew how it worked and friends had one, which meant we could copy pirated games from each other. And it ran
Deluxe Paint
, an era defining graphics program and a killer application for anyone with artistic inclinations, which I'd convinced myself I had.
I had also come into contact with other types of machines. The C64 felt like a thing of the past, with blocky graphics and beepy sound. The Mac was a boring monochrome computer made for writing equally boring documents about tax deductions. I intensely remember seeing a PC for the first time, and how disappointed it made me: it was much worse than the Mac, possibly even than the C64. Downright ugly graphics, terrible sound and a mysterious operating system that required you to learn textual incantations by heart.
But the real home computer feud during those days was between the Amiga 500 and the Atari ST, in which the latter always seemed to come out losing; worse sound, worse graphics, worse OS. Such a machine was completely out of the question - it just
had
to be an Amiga.
I don't regret this decision one bit. Few gadgets have given me as much joy and positive experiences as my Amigas, and even in 1992 an Amiga 500 wasn't a bad purchase. The PC was still a fairly boring machine, having a hard time keeping up with the Amiga's sound and graphics without costing an exorbitant amount of money. The revolutionary Amiga architecture, released in 1985 and basically unchanged since then, could still hold its own: a testament to its ingenuity.
The Price is Right
Around this time, PC:s were showing signs of becoming affordable, and Amiga style platform- and arcade games had begun appearing on the platform. But even the most straightforward of these titles required a fast 386 CPU, plenty of memory and a VGA card to come close to the amount of motion and commotion the Amiga had been capable of for ages. This meant the price to play was still high: In Sweden, around Christmas 1992, a 25 MHz 386/SX with 2 megs of RAM and a 40 meg hard drive was selling for $530. To this came the additional cost of a sound card. A Sound Blaster 2.0, guaranteed to be supported by most games, was available for a whopping $129. While you could hook the Amiga to a cheap 14" TV via RGB SCART, the PC required an expensive VGA monitor, on which you couldn't also watch MacGyver. Bummer!
Shadow of the Beast, released for the Amiga in 1989. It featured
lush graphics, multiple layers of parallax scrolling, massive sprites
and tough as nails gameplay. It looked like crap on pretty much every
other system, and wasn't even ported to the then inferior PC.
This put the cost of an entry level 386 system at $660 without software, compared to the Amiga 600's $499, and the A600's 40 MB hard drive came pre-loaded with Deluxe Paint, a word processor and several decent games. It's true that a 386 PC was much faster than the 7 MHz Amiga in some aspects, but most of those aspects didn't matter for people like me and my friends - at least not yet.
More Moore
It's hard to convey just how intense the effects of Moore's law were during the 90's. When it came to hardware, December 1992 was a
very
different time compared to January 1992. During this year, Commodore pulled a stunt by first introducing the A500+ and then swiftly replacing it with the A600 - a low cost model with the advantage of having an integrated IDE interface, only to finish off by making the A600 obsolete with the release of the next-generation A1200. They were widely criticized for this, but in their defense, home computing was moving at breakneck speed and nobody could really keep up. At any given moment, something that had been unfeasible just six months ago was suddenly commonplace. One such something was
Doom
- which was nowhere, and then suddenly everywhere. Some Amiga fanatics still claim that Doom was what killed the Amiga, but I don't believe that to be true. Doom was a symptom, not the disease proper.

data.title: Where is my von Braun wheel?
data.author: speckx
data.article_summary: 这篇文章探讨了为何NASA在1962年放弃了旋转轮形空间站的研发，转而专注于阿波罗登月计划，导致人工重力空间站的设想被搁置。文章指出，这一历史性决策导致了之后长达半个世纪的小型零重力空间站的模式，给宇航员带来肌肉萎缩、骨质流失和视力问题等健康挑战。早期太空先驱如冯·布劳恩曾认为人工重力对长期太空生活至关重要，其设计的旋转轮形空间站本可实现这一目标。然而，建造大型旋转空间站面临工程挑战，需要解决如何将巨大结构装入细长火箭的难题。文章最后提到，商业航天公司如今重新考虑人工重力站的可能性，或能纠正这一历史性偏差，推动人类成为太空文明。

Where is my von Braun wheel?
Completion: 95%
3604 words
Essay first planted: March 25, 2025 • Last updated: July 3, 2025
In 1962. There — that answers the clickbaity title right away.
NASA had viable designs for rotating wheel space stations that could have given astronauts artificial gravity. Then, the Apollo program effectively killed them.
While NASA’s lunar focus delivered the historic moonshot, it dismantled a promising engineering effort at Langley Research Center that might have revolutionized human spaceflight. That decision set us on a half-century trajectory of small, zero-gravity stations that continue to plague astronauts with
muscle atrophy
,
bone loss
, and
vision problems
.
Had NASA maintained its parallel pursuit of artificial gravity, we might now have permanent orbital settlements supporting deep space missions rather than the limited outposts we’ve settled for. This historical pivot point matters today as commercial space companies contemplate artificial gravity again, potentially correcting a costly detour in humanity’s path to becoming a spacefaring civilisation.
James Webb, the former NASA administrator immortalised by the JWST, standing underneath a prototype of a von Braun Wheel
The need for artificial gravity
Early space visionaries, such as Werner von Braun, strongly believed that settling the solar system required developing technologies to generate artificial gravity within orbiting habitats as — rephrasing
Heinlein
— space is a harsh mistress. Modern-day astronauts
exercise a few hours each day
to overcome
microgravity
’s effects on
the body
. Von Braun was convinced that rotating wheel space stations prevented such physiological problems and were thus “
as inevitable as the rising sun
”. In these systems, humans live along the periphery of a wheel, within which they experience gravity due to the wheel’s rotation. Popularised by von Braun in his 1949 sci-fi novel,
Project Mars
, and the
1956 Disney piece
, the concept actually traces back to
Herman Potočnik
’s 1929 book
The Problem of Space Travel
. Its legacy is perhaps why many felt that an operational spinning station was, at best, a couple decades away.

.
Potočnik’s first conceptualised the rotating space station.
von Braun explaining the layout of his wheel-shaped station
The difficulty of building large stations
⊕
Rotational forces applied to wine tasting.
This elegant solution to generate artificial gravity, however, comes with a major engineering challenge. Much like a ferris wheel, the wheel’s rotation could disorient astronauts if spun too fast. If the wheel spins slowly then its physics dictates it must be quite large. For example, one of von Braun’s designs called for a massive 75 metre diameter wheel that generated lunar gravity if spun at 3 rpm and Earth-like gravity at 5 rpm — this range is considered
reasonable for astronauts
.
However, the physics of rockets presents a different obstacle as it must be slender, like an arrow, to escape Earth’s gravity well and reach orbit. This defines the main upstream engineering challenge: how can we fit enormous space structures into slender rockets? For context, even Starship’s
upper-stage
, which is about 9 metres wide and 22 metres tall cannot fit von Braun’s conceptual station in a straightforward manner.
Architects of the International Space Station (ISS), the largest space structure ever built, tackled a similar packing problem using multiple smaller spacecraft which connect, like space Ikea, into a structure greater than its parts. Such in-space assembly involves spacecraft either gently crashing into each other at specific connection points (a manoeuvre called
rendezvous and docking
) as well as
astronauts and space cranes
supporting finer assembly tasks. While this works great in theory, the ISS’s assembly needed over 40 rocket launches spanning several years (and even more launches for cargo resupply and repairs). More damning is the typical ISS crew size of 7, which is a little over twice that of the first ever space station, Salyut, from 1972. Clearly 50 years of space station development does not indicate that such modular in-orbit assembly will scale to von Braun’s
anticipated 80 humans
or, more relevant today, Starship’s
100
any time soon. Civilisation-scale megastructures like the Stanford Torus and O’Neill cylinders appear even more outlandish to discuss today than when they were first proposed in the 70s.
The Stanford Torus concept for 10,000 space settlers was proposed during the 1975 NASA Summer Study.
The O’Neill cylinder was proposed in 1976 by Gerard O’Neill.
From this vantage point, it is quite clear that the architectural bottleneck is a technology running through all operational space stations so far: their use of small ‘tin can’ modular spacecraft as the centrepiece for assembly, which is a legacy of Apollo. This, in my opinion, is unfit

data.title: Spending Too Much Money on a Coding Agent
data.author: GavinAnderegg
data.article_summary: 作者Allen Pike分享了他在使用大型语言模型进行编程的经历。起初，他使用Anthropic的Claude Sonnet进行日常编码，虽然模型表现不错，但在时间压力下，模型的不足（如过度复杂化修改和提出不必要的依赖）让他感到沮丧。于是他尝试了更大型但缓慢的模型o3，尽管成本高昂，他发现o3在工具使用、进展评估和自我修正方面表现出色，实际效果优于预期。尽管每个对话平均花费约5美元，每天约50美元，作者和联合创始人Jenn决定在三周内增加预算至1000美元/月，最终发现效果显著。作者提供了如何从这类模型获得更高价值的建议，如尽早发现错误和使用成熟技术。多位业内人士也认同这种高成本模型的价值。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕AI工具（尤其是基于LLM的编码工具）的使用成本、价值和未来发展的讨论。

不同观点：
• iamleppert：对依赖第三方公司提供的AI工具来创建公司的可持续性表示担忧。认为如果这些工具突然被撤回（rug pull），公司将陷入困境，因为没有内部团队支持。
• jbentley1：分享了自己使用Claude Code工具的经历，通过开发工具实现了高效的并行会话处理，认为这些工具在正确工具支持下能提供巨大价值。
• pshirshov：反对只使用“无聊的技术”，认为推动新技术（如Haskell和WebAssembly）的发展是有意义的，否则未来可能没有新的技术突破。
• rogerkirkness：作为早期创始人的观点，认为每月200美元的成本相对于雇佣工程师的费用是非常值得的，是公司目前最高回报的投资。
• mathiaspoint：无法想象不自我托管的情况下使用这些工具，认为在编辑器中操作不应该收费，否则会严重影响工作效率。

• lvl155：认为200美元/月的费用在能大幅提高生产力的情况下是值得的，时间是最宝贵的资源。
• jasonthorsness：希望避免长期的计量收费模式，认为当前AI工具的成本正在威胁软件开发的低资本进入壁垒。
• feintruled：对Agentic AI工具的发展表示兴趣，但质疑其底层技术的实际效果。
• quonn：认为200美元/月的收费只有在没有真正的市场竞争或垄断的情况下才可能持续，预期价格会因为竞争而下降。
• georgeecollins：惊讶于可以用10k/月雇佣到创始工程师，认为优秀工程师的价值很高。
• hoistbypetard：批评将失败的测试改为跳过的测试以解决问题的方式，认为这像是一个非常自信但缺乏经验的初级开发者。

• tabs_or_spaces：认为讨论主要集中在开发成本的节省上，但没有提及使用AI编码工具对收入和新客户产生的实际影响。

补充讨论：
- 争议焦点：AI工具的收费模式和未来价格趋势。一些人认为当前的高价不可持续，而另一些人则认为其带来的生产力提升足以抵消成本。
- 另一个值得注意的点是关于使用AI工具的效率问题，部分用户（如jbentley1和chis）分享了具体工具的使用经验和策略，以最大化工具的价值。
- 关于技术选择的问题，pshirshov主张推动新技术发展，而iamleppert则担心过度依赖现有AI工具的风险。
- 最后，关于个人和公司使用AI工具的成本负担问题，bicepjai和quonn提出了对更合理定价的需求。

Allen Pike

Spending Too Much Money on a Coding Agent
On making use of large thinking models.
June 30, 2025 •
7 min read
For a year, I’d been coding almost every day with Cursor and Claude Sonnet. Anthropic’s 3.5 and 3.7 Sonnet each rightly earned their dominant place on the
programming model charts
: they were the least-bad coding models yet.
In the earliest days of LLMs, there was tremendous interest in ever-larger model releases. Hype around bigger, slower models has since waned, as Claude 3 Opus, GPT 4.5, and OpenAI o1 – all large and technically impressive model releases, each useful for some niche purposes – were ultimately too expensive and slow to be worth the squeeze for day-to-day coding.
But then, this spring, something interesting happened.
Full speed ahead
Last month, my co-founder Jenn and I were rapidly sprinting to hit a self-imposed deadline (demoing our latest experiment at Web Summit Vancouver). Luckily, Claude Sonnet is truly helpful when coding – especially in TypeScript. Still, under time pressure, I started to get annoyed with its LLM-isms: overcomplicating changes, proposing unnecessary dependencies, and just
literally changing failing tests into skipped tests
to resolve “the tests are failing.” Like, what the crap?
Frustrated, I tried switching from Claude Sonnet to the new o3 thinking model. I knew o3 was painfully slow, so I took the time to write out exactly what I knew, and what I wanted the solution to look like, and gave it some time to work. To my surprise, the response was… great?
The more I tried it, the more I found o3’s improved ability to use tools, assess progress, and self-correct led to results that were actually worth the wait. I found myself expanding what terminal commands I allowed the agent to run, helping it get further than ever before. When I completed a hard “o3-grade” task and moved on to something simpler, I was increasingly tempted to leave it on o3 instead of switching back. Sonnet was faster in theory. But o3 was faster in practice.
The only problem was, it was costing a fortune.
Depending on the task, my o3 conversations were averaging roughly $5 of Cursor requests each, or about $50 a day. That… is a lot of money.
Still, we were in a hurry. And what is a startup if not a series of experiments? So I turned to my co-founder.
Jenn, I have a proposal. You’re going to hate it.
I’m listening?
So you know I’ve been getting really good results from o3. I propose we try just defaulting to o3 for the next 3 weeks until our demo, and increase our Cursor spending cap to $1000/mo.
That’s a
lot
of money.
I know. It’s ridiculous. This is ridiculous. But also, when we hire a Founding Engineer, they will cost a lot more than that. Like, 10x more.
…Okay. Let’s try it. If it’s not worth the cost, we’ll go back.
So we tried it. And, to both of our horror, it was worth the cost.
We’ve found that compared to Claude 4 Sonnet and GPT-4.1, large thinking models like Claude 4 Opus and especially OpenAI o3 will:
More successfully use tools like MCPs and CLIs to troubleshoot issues
Less often propose overlarge patches that add risk or tech debt
More often find relevant code, instead of duplicating things
Less often “reward hack” by commenting out tests or otherwise being a dolt
Be a more effective research partner when weighing potential tech approaches
Follow our Cursor rules more diligently, including the rule not to try adding npm dependencies that don’t even flippin’ exist, you complete dingbat
Still. $1000/mo is insane. So I’ve been keeping an eye out for somebody to convince me we’re crazy.
Instead, in early June
Andrej Karpathy claimed
:
o3 is the obvious best [model] for important/hard things.
At a software company, coding counts as important. A couple days later, the Head of Engineering at Shopify
cited a coding model budget of $1k/month/dev
as being “cheap”.
Emboldened, I decided to test the water by mentioning to one of our investors – a co-founder at a relatively large tech company – that we were trialling spending $1000/mo on o3 inference.
$1000/mo! What are you doing with o3 that’s costing that much? I’m averaging $50/day on Claude Opus 4
$50/day is $1000/mo?
Oh lol right, yeah you’re good
So I guess it really is a thing. You can get $1000/mo of value from coding agents now.
How to get $1000/mo of value from coding agents
Obviously, simply spending $1000 does not guarantee you a positive return! Here are some practices that we’ve found get more value out of large thinking models like o3 and Claude Opus:
Shift errors earlier
: The faster you can detect a coding error, the cheaper it is to fix. This is doubly true for LLMs. Shifting errors from runtime → test-time → build-time makes everybody more productive. Even better, fix issues deterministically with a linter or formatter. Let your expensive LLMs and humans focus on the squishy parts.

: LLMs do much better with well-documented and well-understood dependencies than obscur

data.title: Opening up ‘Zero-Knowledge Proof’ technology
data.author: doomroot13
data.article_summary: 谷歌开源了其零知识证明（ZKP）库，以增强隐私保护，特别是在年龄验证方面。ZKP技术允许用户证明某些信息为真，而无需分享其他数据，例如在不需要透露其他信息的情况下证明自己年满18岁。通过开放这些加密工具的源代码，谷歌旨在帮助公共和私营部门的开发者构建更注重隐私的应用和数字身份解决方案。这不仅有利于用户享有更私密和安全的数字环境，还帮助企业和研究人员满足隐私需求并开发新应用。此举也响应了欧盟即将于2026年生效的eIDAS法规，鼓励成员国在欧洲数字身份钱包中采用增强隐私的技术。源代码可在GitHub上获取。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：非交互式零知识证明（Zero-Knowledge Proofs, ZKPs）的直觉解释及其应用

不同观点：
• **对非交互式零知识证明的直观理解需求**：[bobbiechen] 提到对交互式零知识证明有较好的理解，但难以找到对非交互式零知识证明的直观解释，并提供了一些参考资料。
• **隐私与身份验证的应用**：[natch] 认为零知识证明可以在保护隐私的前提下解决许多因过度分享个人信息（PII）导致的问题，例如使用社会保障号码（SSNs）。
• **技术实现与安全性争议**：[csense] 提出如何防御通过未经授权的方式获取私钥并绕过验证手段的攻击。

补充讨论：
• **零知识证明的历史与商业化**：[ChuckMcM] 回顾了零知识证明技术在90年代的商业化尝试，如DigiCash和Andy Birrell的微支付概念，并表达了对这些技术重新应用的兴趣。
• **复杂性与应用限制**：[Confiks] 讨论了一种复杂的多展示无关性与硬件绑定的解决方案，指出其复杂性和应用限制，并提到绕过验证的潜在方法。
• **去中心化身份验证的潜力**：[esbranson] 认为零知识证明可以用于去中心化身份验证，例如在不提供个人信息的情况下验证政治党派 affiliation。
• **技术扩展与应用场景**：[est] 询问是否可以通过零知识证明验证电子邮件地址的有效性。[vvpan] 提到 zkTLS 技术可以在不透露用户名的情况下证明拥有某个在线服务的账户。

争议焦点：
• **隐私保护与绕过验证的可能性**：[Confiks] 与 [csense] 都提到即使有隐私保护机制，验证系统仍可能被绕过，强调需要设定合理的期望。
• **技术的创新性与实用性**：[hrdwdmrbl] 质疑该技术是否在当前研究前沿仍具有创新性和实用性，或者已经被其他团队超越。

其他值得注意的讨论点：
• **具体应用场景的讨论**：[Labo333] 提到在法国和美国一些州，成人内容网站因难以实现年龄验证而受到影响。[baby] 分享了关于零知识证明的资讯平台。[mumbisChungo] 提到零知识证明在分布式网络中保护信息隐私的应用。[ranger_danger] 质疑零知识证明如何验证请求来自真人而非机器人。
• **潜在商业应用**：[cyberax] 提出该技术可能实现类似Scroll的匿名付费浏览网络。

总结：讨论主要围绕非交互式零知识证明的直观理解、技术实现与安全性、隐私保护与绕过验证的可能性、以及该技术在不同场景下的应用潜力与限制。

Today, we open sourced our

, fulfilling a
promise
and building on our
partnership with Sparkasse
to support
EU age assurance
.
Open sourcing these powerful cryptographic tools will make it much easier for private and public sector developers to build their own privacy-enhancing applications and digital ID solutions, meeting an urgent need.
In layperson’s terms, ZKP makes it possible for people to prove that something about them is
true
without exchanging any other data. So, for example, a person visiting a website can verifiably prove he or she is over 18, without sharing anything else at all.
The goal of sharing ZKP with the open source and cryptography communities reflects our commitment to helping
all
parties in the ecosystem:
Web and app users benefit from being inhabitants of a more private and secure digital ecosystem.
Businesses and other relying organizations of all sizes can easily leverage this open source solution to meet their privacy needs.
Developers can freely use the ZKP codebase to build privacy-focused applications.
Researchers can use this more efficient and performant ZKP implementation to help create new applications and uses of technology.
The European Union’s eIDAS Regulation set to take effect in 2026 encourages Member States to integrate privacy-enhancing technologies like ZKP into the European Digital Identity Wallet (“EUDI Wallet”). With our commitment to making these ZKP tools openly available, Member States can integrate this into their future EUDI Wallets, accelerating their development.
We're so excited for this new chapter for Zero-Knowledge Proofs and invite you to explore the ZKP codebase on

data.title: Launch HN: K-Scale Labs (YC W24) – Open-Source Humanoid Robots
data.author: codekansas
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕一款新推出的开源人形机器人，各方对技术、市场和应用前景的讨论。

不同观点：
• **对开源和现有技术的质疑**：BrandiATMuhkuh 对项目选择开源和未使用 ROS（机器人操作系统）等现有项目表示疑惑，询问是否因为这些技术已经过时。这表明部分专业人士对重新开发基础技术持怀疑态度，认为可能不需要“重启”此类项目。
  
• **对双足机器人稳定性的担忧**：BrandiATMuhkuh 基于过去的实验经验，认为双足机器人存在稳定性差、漂移严重的问题，并质疑选择双足而非四足设计的原因。这反映了对双足机器人实际应用中的技术瓶颈的担忧。

• **对机器人脚部设计的讨论**：chrsw 提出为什么大多数 humanoid 机器人没有类似人类足部的关节（如跖趾关节），并指出人类足部的柔性和神经末梢对机器人移动性能的重要性。这涉及对机器人仿生设计和硬件局限性的讨论。

• **对全自主机器人的算法和市场质疑**：randomNumber7 质疑项目方在全自主机器人中使用的机器学习算法，并指出硬件易得、控制难，特别是如何吸引开发者贡献开源代码。同时，也表达了对市场前景的担忧，认为消费者不一定会为开源代码买单。

• **对市场定位和消费动机的分析**：v5v3 认为当前购买人形机器人的消费者多出于对“女性形象”机器人的兴趣，而非功能性需求。这指向了一个较为细分甚至带有性别刻板印象的消费市场。

• **对市场需求和融资策略的讨论**：markisus 提出该项目面临“为技术找应用场景”的问题，并质疑其市场潜力。同时，对项目如何获得投资表示好奇。这反映了技术创业中常见的市场不确定性问题。

• **对价格和实际应用的讨论**：deepdarkforest 认为当前人形机器人实用性不足，并质疑项目方在未完全实现自主功能前的高价销售策略。这与 ZeroCool2u 对价格的积极评价形成对比，表明消费者对价格和实际功能的敏感度不同。

补充讨论：
• **对机器人硬件和软件开发的平衡**：accurrent 和 dbmikus 都提到了与现有竞争对手（如中国的 Unitree）的比较，关注项目方在硬件和软件开发上的资源分配，尤其是如何在市场竞争中取得优势。

• **对机器人手部设计的期待**：lachyg 关注机器人手部的设计，询问何时能出现价格合理且性能可靠的多指机械手，反映了业界对精细操作能力的需求。

• **对不同配置和升级的疑问**：dan344 和 fragmede 都对机器人不同配置的价格和性能差异提出疑问，特别是 $3000 的差价包含哪些额外功能，这涉及消费者对产品性价比的关注。

• **对开源项目的实际参与**：pj_mukh 表示没有足够时间和预算参与硬件开发，但希望了解项目中开放的软件问题，显示了对开源项目不同参与程度的兴趣。

争议焦点：
• **双足设计的可行性和市场定位**：部分讨论者质疑双足设计的实际效果和市场需求，认为四足或其他设计可能更稳定和实用。
• **高价与功能性不匹配**：一些评论者认为当前人形机器人在未完全实现自主功能的情况下，售价过高，难以吸引广泛市场。

总结：讨论围绕技术实现、市场需求、价格策略和消费者动机展开，显示了人形机器人在技术、市场和消费层面的多重挑战。
