44457818.article_content:
We got two big pieces of energy news from Google this week. The company announced that it’s signed an agreement to purchase electricity from a fusion company’s forthcoming first power plant. Google also released its latest environmental report, which shows that
its energy use from data centers has
doubled
since 2020
.
Taken together, these two bits of news offer a fascinating look at just how desperately big tech companies are hunting for clean electricity to power their data centers as energy demand and emissions balloon in the age of AI. Of course, we don’t know exactly how much of this pollution is attributable to AI because Google doesn’t break that out. (Also a problem!) So, what’s next and what does this all mean?
Related Story
Inside a fusion energy facility
Commonwealth Fusion Systems is trying to bring a long-promised technology to reality.
Let’s start with fusion: Google’s
deal with Commonwealth Fusion Systems
is intended to provide the tech giant with 200 megawatts of power. This will come from Commonwealth’s first commercial plant, a facility planned for Virginia that the company refers to as the Arc power plant. The agreement represents half its capacity.
What’s important to note here is that this power plant doesn’t exist yet. In fact, Commonwealth still needs to get its Sparc demonstration reactor, located outside Boston, up and running. That site,
which I visited in the fall
, should be completed in 2026.
(An aside: This isn’t the first deal between Big Tech and a fusion company. Microsoft signed an agreement with Helion a couple of years ago to buy 50 megawatts of power from a planned power plant, scheduled to come online in 2028. Experts expressed skepticism in the wake of that deal,
as my colleague James Temple reported
.)
Nonetheless, Google’s announcement is a big moment for fusion, in part because of the size of the commitment and also because Commonwealth, a spinout company from MIT’s Plasma Science and Fusion Center, is seen by many in the industry as a likely candidate to be the first to get a commercial plant off the ground. (
MIT Technology Review
is owned by MIT but is editorially independent.)
Google leadership was very up-front about the length of the timeline. “We would certainly put this in the long-term category,” said Michael Terrell, Google’s head of advanced energy, in a press call about the deal.
The news of Google’s foray into fusion comes just days after the tech giant’s release of its latest environmental report. While the company highlighted some wins, some of the numbers in this report are eye-catching, and not in a positive way.
Google’s emissions have increased by over 50% since 2019
, rising 6% in the last year alone. That’s decidedly the wrong direction for a company that’s set a goal to reach net-zero greenhouse-gas emissions by the end of the decade.
It’s true that the company has committed billions to clean energy projects, including big investments in next-generation technologies like advanced nuclear and enhanced geothermal systems. Those deals have helped dampen emissions growth, but it’s an arguably impossible task to keep up with the energy demand the company is seeing.
Google’s electricity consumption from data centers was up 27% from the year before. It’s
doubled
since 2020, reaching over 30 terawatt-hours.
That’s nearly the annual electricity consumption from the entire country of
Ireland
.
As an outsider, it’s tempting to point the finger at AI, since that technology has crashed into the mainstream and percolated into every corner of Google’s products and business. And yet the report downplays the role of AI. Here’s one bit that struck me:
“However, it’s important to note that our growing electricity needs aren’t solely driven by AI. The accelerating growth of Google Cloud, continued investments in Search, the expanding reach of YouTube, and more, have also contributed to this overall growth.”
There is enough wiggle room in that statement to drive a large electric truck through. When I asked about the relative contributions here, company representative Mara Harris said via email that they don’t break out what portion comes from AI. When I followed up asking if the company didn’t have this information or just wouldn’t share it, she said she’d check but didn’t get back to me.
I’ll make the point here that we’ve made before, including in
our recent package on AI and energy
:
Big companies should be disclosing more about the energy demands of AI. We shouldn’t be guessing at this technology’s effects.
Google has put a ton of effort and resources into setting and chasing ambitious climate goals. But as its energy needs and those of the rest of the industry continue to explode, it’s obvious that this problem is getting tougher, and it’s also clear that more transparency is a crucial part of the way forward.

44458398.article_content:
DETROIT
Detroit sues blockchain real estate firm that owns rentals with hundreds of violations
Nushrat Rahman
Detroit Free Press
Hear this story
The firms sell "fractional ownership" in Detroit rental properties.
The city's top lawyer called the complaint the biggest nuisance abatement lawsuit it has ever filed.
An apartment building with fire damage. A home without heat or smoke detectors. Multiple properties with broken windows.
Over on the east side, a Detroiter living in her home without running water for two months, forcing her to survive off of bottles of water. Another tenant living upstairs in the same apartment complex with no hot water in her kitchen, electrical sockets that don't work and gaps in her windows. Outside of their home, a backyard door that appears boarded shut.
These are among the properties, and living conditions, at the center of a sprawling lawsuit filed by the city of Detroit on July 2 against Real Token, a Florida-based blockchain real estate company; its co-founders, brothers Remy Jacobson and Jean-Marc Jacobson, and 165 affiliates, for public nuisance violations involving more than 400 residential properties in Detroit.
"This is the largest nuisance abatement lawsuit ever filed by the city of Detroit," said Conrad Mallett, corporation counsel for the city of Detroit, speaking at a news conference on the city's west side near one of the many properties cited in the suit.
At issue: Real Token, or RealT, is operating a cryptocurrency venture in Detroit, involving dozens of limited liability companies and related entities, by offering international investors "fractional ownership of Detroit properties represented as digital tokens," according to the suit. The city of Detroit, in its complaint, alleges that its tenants — Detroit residents — are paying the price with poorly maintained rental properties and unsanitary and unsafe conditions. The city's lawsuit follows an
Outlier Media investigation
published earlier this year about the company.
"Behind the high tech language lies a deeply familiar problem in this city, and that is neglected properties ... unresponsive management, and Detroit families, many of them single mothers, left to live in unsafe and unhealthy conditions. Tenants have reported persistent mold, broken plumbing, caved-in ceilings and a total lack of basic maintenance, yet their rent is still being collected," said District 2 Council Member Angela Whitfield-Calloway.
On its
website
, Real Token says "for the first time, investors around the globe can buy into the US real estate market through fully-compliant, fractional, tokenized ownership." Since 2019, the company says it has garnered more than 65,000 registered investors. Ownership of property is spread out across "representative tokens" and owners "can collect revenue from rent, and vote on property decisions," according to the company's website. Each property has a management company that "sources tenants, collects rent, and manages repairs, so the diverse group of RealToken owners don’t have to."
In a statement, RealToken, laid the blame on management companies it hired for the properties.
"Since RealToken has entered the Detroit market, we have been committed to the goal of providing safe, affordable housing for our tenants, and playing a supporting role in revitalizing Detroit's neighborhoods. Unfortunately, we have been one of many victims in Detroit of several unscrupulous property management companies. These companies were paid hundreds of thousands of dollars to oversee RealToken’s properties, address tenant complaints and make repairs, and maintain each of our properties in accordance with City of Detroit municipal codes. As it turns out, there are many instances where these goals were not achieved, and each management company, in its own way, stole these funds to the detriment of RealToken and more importantly, the tenants we serve," according to a statement from the company provided to the Free Press on July 3 issued through Cadence, a Detroit-based communications firm.
The statement went on to say: "We took over all the properties at once and started addressing blight violations, administrative filings, servicing maintenance calls and conducting full rehabs. We have made complete repairs to over several dozens of properties, addressed hundreds of blight tickets, and have contractor teams in the field every day addressing each disgruntled tenant and city citation in turn. This process cannot happen overnight. It takes time. But we are committed to addressing every issue, and finally execute on our original mission."
Real Token has not been served a lawsuit, according to the company, and reserved further comment.

data.title: A list is a monad
data.author: polygot
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了函数式编程中“单子”（monad）的概念，指出常见解释往往在抽象比喻和数学抽象之间摇摆，难以兼顾直观性和精确性。单子可以被视为一种“容器”或“延迟计算”，主要用于在不同计算上下文中复用函数，而无需重写控制流逻辑。文章将单子分为两类：“结果”型单子（如List、Maybe）和“配方”型单子（如C#中的Task）。结果型单子代表已计算的值和其上下文，而配方型单子则代表尚未发生的计算。文章详细介绍了List单子的map和flatMap操作，并对比了面向对象编程中处理数据结构的繁琐过程，强调单子通过统一接口简化了逻辑的组合与执行。文章最后表示将进一步探讨“配方”型单子。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对Monad概念及其解释方法的不同看法

不同观点：
• brooke2k认为，现有的Monad教程往往让学习者更困惑，因为它们聚焦于错误的内容。Monad本身并不复杂，每个Monad实例的应用方式各不相同，应该为每个常见实例（如Maybe、IO、State等）单独讲解。同时，Monad在Haskell中的表现比在其他语言中更直观，因为Haskell的符号更简洁，且支持类型类。

• kevinventullo从C++的模板角度解释Monad，将其类比为一个模板类T，具有特定的三个方法（F、G、T<f>），并指出这种结构满足某些兼容性规则。他认为这种数学化的解释虽然有些复杂，但大多数自然构造都会满足这些要求。

• nemo1618反对将列表直接称为Monad，指出列表是一种数据结构，而Monad更像是一种“特质”或“接口”。Haskell中的列表Monad是对非确定性建模的一种选择，而非列表本身固有的属性。

• gr4vityWall认为最直观的Monad描述是'flatMappable'，并提到如果用非常数学化的方式解释会让人更困惑。他指出这篇文章比其他文章更易理解，但在结尾部分仍显复杂。

• kerblang将Monad视为解决回调地狱的工具，通过Monad函数创建“for comprehensions”来简化嵌套回调，使代码更具可读性。

• robinhouston指出，从数学角度看，列表并不是Monad，列表是一种Monad，列表的代数是该Monad的代数。

• t43562认为，现有的Monad解释往往让人更难理解，强调Monad能做什么比Monad是什么更重要，且Haskell的解释方式需要先了解它解决的问题。

• 1-more补充，Map是函子的属性，每个Monad都是函子，且每个Monad都是Applicative函子。Monad总是有Map，但不需要Monad就可以有Map。

• ivanjermakov指出，列表可以是Monad的一种实例，理解Monad的关键在于其提供的接口优势。

• drumnerd强调，Monad不是容器，而是一种组合带有效果的函数的方式，通过注入值和组合函数来实现。

• tombert表示，意识到列表是Monad让他理解了Monad，将其视为带有上下文的值，并指出理解这一点可以打开重用性的大门。

• benreesman从编译器和程序执行语义的角度讨论Monad，指出Monad是一种描述程序执行语义的数学对象。

• kelseyfrog反对简单地说“列表是Monad”，指出更准确的表述应是“列表可以被赋予Monad实例”等，并提到Monad的理解是一种主观体验。

• acjohnson55将列表Monad视为“离散非确定性Monad”，通过flatMap操作返回新的可能输出集合，并指出这种扩展在其他领域仍然适用。

• skybrian将Monad视为一种设计模式，用于构造新对象并传递回调函数，强调Monad的bind操作是添加回调并控制流。

补充讨论：
- Monad教程的有效性及其对学习者的影响是争议焦点。
- 不同背景（数学、编程语言）的人对Monad的理解和解释方式各异。
- 强调Monad能做什么比Monad是什么更有助于理解。
- 对列表是否是Monad及其相关属性有不同看法。
- 强调Monad的理解是一种主观体验，需通过实践获得。

44414965.article_content:
This post got a lot more interest than expected! Currently working on revising this post to incorporate the excellent suggestions from Hacker News. Having said that, please still provide feedback.
The term “monad” is often invoked when describing patterns in functional programming. Yet explanations typically swing between high-level metaphors and deep mathematical abstractions. Each approach offers part of the picture, intuition without precision, or rigor without intuition but seldom both.
Monads can be
idealized
as a
container
(albeit is
a flawed metaphor
) or context holding a value (or multiple values, or no value),
but in some cases we will get into later on
it’s better to think of it as a
recipe
or
deferred computation
for producing a value. At the heart of monadic programming is the idea that you write
one
function, say,
f(x) = x + 1
, and then
reuse
it across different contexts without rewriting control-flow logic.
Two Flavours: Result vs Recipe
While all monads provide a computational context, they generally fall into two flavors:
Monads as “Results”: These represent a value that has already been computed, but with extra context.
List<int>
is a result with the context.
Maybe<int>
is the result of a computation with the context of “possible optionalness.” For these, the “container” metaphor is a useful, if limited, starting point.
Monads as “Recipes”: These represent a computation that has not happened yet. They are a blueprint for producing a value. C#’s
Task<T>
is a perfect example: it doesn’t hold a value, it holds the promise of a value to be computed asynchronously. For these, the “recipe” metaphor is a much better fit. Unwrapping a task doesn’t give you the computed result, it just gives you the instructions
to
compute it.
Sometimes, you can mix the flavors. In this post, we will focus on the first category to build our core intuition. We’ll start with
List
and
Maybe
to understand the mechanics of
map
and
flatMap
on concrete results. In Part 2, we’ll see how these same patterns unlock immense power when applied to “recipe” monads like
Task
.
List
: Map & FlatMap in Practice
To an OOP developer, monadic types (
List<T>
) might look just like generics. It’s a typical pitfall to think “we have generics, so we have monads,” which isn’t true by itself. Monads do usually involve generic types, but they
require specific operations (Unit and flatMap) and the three monad laws on those types to ensure uniform behavior.
This is key
and is fundamental to working with monads.
A good example of a monad is a list. You’re likely very familiar with lists and working with lists.
The monad Map operation is responsible for:
Applying your function.
For a
List
,
Map
runs
f
on
every
element, so the list
[0,1,2,3]
becomes
[1,2,3,4]
. If the list doesn’t have any elements, then, well,
Map
doesn’t call
f
.
f
doesn’t need to worry about that. Also,
f
doesn’t care if it’s a list, all
f
is, is just
f(x) = x + 1
.
Map
is responsible for running it.
Managing sequencing and combination.
The list context concatenates results into one list. We don’t need to manually modify or re-add elements to the list via
Add
.
Notice that the monad is responsible for running
f(x)
. This shift means your business logic stays
declarative
and
composable
, you describe
what
happens to a single value, and the monad describes
how
and
when
it happens.
This is different from OO and procedural programming because in procedural programming, if you want to process data, it is your responsibility to understand how to apply the function to your data. We have to use different control constructs to handle different types of data, and are also responsible for the “how”.

userInput

)

// userInput could still be null here, or, it could be the concatenated result
// 3. Dictionary<string, string>: you must know it’s key/value pairs

=

**XORSATFilter** 是一个由美国国家安全局（NSA）发布的库，用于构建高效的集合成员过滤器和字典，基于可满足性问题（Satisfiability problem）。与 Bloom 过滤器不同，k-XORSAT 过滤器是静态的，即一旦构建就无法添加新元素，但其内存使用接近最优，比 Bloom 过滤器更节省空间。k-XORSAT 过滤器在查询速度上与 Bloom 过滤器相当，且在低误报率下速度更快。

该库依赖于 pthreads 和标准 C 数学库，并包含一些 git 子模块。安装过程通过运行 `make` 完成，库文件 `libxorsatfilter.a` 将在 `lib` 目录下生成。

使用时，k-XORSAT 过滤器的构建分为两个阶段：首先向构建器对象添加元素，然后从构建器创建查询器对象。查询器可无限次查询。

元素添加示例：
```c
XORSATFilterBuilder *xsfb = XORSATFilterBuilderAlloc(0, 0);
XORSATFilterBuilderAddElement(xsfb, pElement, nElementBytes, pMetaData);
```

完成后创建查询器：
```c
XORSATFilterQuerier *xsfq = XORSATFilterBuilderFinalize(xsfb, XORSATFilterFastParameters, nThreads);
```

其中，`XORSATFilterFastParameters` 等参数可根据需求选择，控制过滤器的构建速度和大小。详细信息见 `include/xorsat_filter.h` 和 `src/xorsat_blocks.c`。

主要讨论点：研究出版物中的许可问题、SAT过滤器的功能及其应用、过滤器技术的效率和实现

不同观点：
• **[gopalv]** 赞赏美国政府研究出版物的无版权许可，但指出SAT过滤器不支持增量构建，这一功能在分布式数据库中是布隆过滤器的一大特色（可以通过构建多个过滤器并进行OR操作来生成单一过滤器）。虽然手动进行OR操作仍能提高准确性，但效率上可能存在问题。

• **[inasio]** 强调了成员过滤器的高效性，尤其是在处理假阳性问题时（假阳性的数量和比例可以根据数据集和过滤器参数调整）。他提到一个明显的应用场景是检查乘客是否在禁飞名单上，这种情况下假阳性可以通过进一步检查来处理。同时，他指出使用SAT或XORSAT求解器可以生成许多可行解决方案，并认为cuckoo过滤器是当前最先进的技术。

• **[convolvatron]** 提到存储库中的一些参考文献被付费墙阻挡，但找到了一个可能相关的免费论文链接。他还指出，该构造与完美哈希有相似之处，这为讨论添加了另一种技术实现的可能性。

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点**：SAT过滤器是否支持增量构建及其在分布式数据库中的应用效率问题。gopalv认为当前不支持增量构建是一个不足，而inasio则关注于SAT求解器在生成解决方案方面的潜力。

• **技术应用**：讨论中提到了过滤器技术在实际应用中的场景，如禁飞名单检查，这为过滤器技术的实际价值提供了具体例子。

• **资源获取**：convolvatron提出了论文获取的付费墙问题，并提供了一个可能相关的免费资源链接，这反映了学术资源获取中的现实问题。

INTRODUCTION
This is a library for building and querying a compressed form of
set-membership filters, named k-XORSAT filters. These filters can be
used similar to how one would use a Bloom filter but with one
restriction --- items cannot be added after the filter is built. So,
this is an 'offline' or 'static' filter, whereas Bloom filters are
considered 'online' or 'dynamic'. The advantage is that k-XORSAT
filters achieve very near the optimal memory usage. That is, they use
much less memory than Bloom filters, making them desirable for either
large data sets (save space) or data sets that are provided to a large
user base (save bandwidth).
The advantage of k-XORSAT filters over other filters with small memory
footprint is that the near-optimal compression of k-XORSAT filters is
reliably achieved, and the query speed is comparable to Bloom filters
for high false positive rates, and faster than Bloom filters for small
false positive rates.
DEPENDENCIES
This package depends on pthreads and standard C math libraries.
This project also relies on a few git submodules. To get these
modules, clone the repository by doing either
git clone --recursive git@github.com:NationalSecurityAgency/XORSATFilter.git
or
git clone git@github.com:NationalSecurityAgency/XORSATFilter.git
cd XORSATFilter
git submodule update --init --recursive
INSTALL
Run
make
in the project root directory. The library file
libxorsatfilter.a
will (assuming successful compilation) be created
in this package's
lib
directory.
USE
k-XORSAT filters are built in two separate phases. The first step is
to add elements to a builder object. The second phase is to create a
querier object from a builder object. Once completed, the querier
object may be queried ad infinitum.
A builder is first allocated using
XORSATFilterBuilderAlloc
,
like so:
XORSATFilterBuilder *xsfb = XORSATFilterBuilderAlloc(0, 0);
Here, the first argument
0
is the number of expected elements the
filter will encode. It is safe to leave this number as
0
, but will
decrease calls to malloc if the number is given ahead of time. The
second argument is the number of bytes of metatdata to store with each
element. To use the data structure as a filter, enter 0. To use the
data structure as a dictionary, enter the number of bytes to store in
the dictionary.
Elements are added to the builder, like so:
XORSATFilterBuilderAddElement(xsfb, pElement, nElementBytes, pMetaData);
Here,
pElement
is a pointer to at least
nElementBytes
number of
bytes. This element will be copied into the builder.
pMetaData
is a
pointer to an array of bytes that will be stored into the data
structure and can be retrieved after construction. If the data
structure is used as a filter, this last argument may be
NULL
.
It is also possible to add the absence of an element to the
filter. This will cause the filter to return
False
when queried
against the element.
XORSATFilterBuilderAddAbsence(xsfb, pElement, nElementBytes);
After all elements have been stored, the querier is ready to be
created:
XORSATFilterQuerier *xsfq = XORSATFilterBuilderFinalize(xsfb, XORSATFilterFastParameters, nThreads);
The second argument is a structure consisting of four parameters: the
number of literals per row, the number of solutions, the number of
elements per block, and the desired efficiency of the filter. Three
samples are provided by the package,
XORSATFilterEfficientParameters
creates small filters but has longer
build time.
XORSATFilterPaperParameters
creates filters according to parameters used in a recent paper on XORSAT filters.
XORSATFilterFastParameters
creates filters quickly but
the filters are larger.
More information can be found near the tops of
include/xorsat_filter.h
and
src/xorsat_blocks.c
. Feel free to
define your own parameters to meet the needs of your application.
The third
nThreads
argument corresponds to the number of pthreads
used when building the querier. The returned querier (
xsfq
) will be
NULL
on error.
When finalizing, you will notice that the progress is printed to
stderr. These print statements can be turned off by commenting out the
following line in xorsat_fi

data.title: Show HN: Jobs by Referral: Find jobs in your LinkedIn network
data.author: nicksergeant
data.article_summary:
JobsByReferral帮助你通过分析专业人脉网络寻找工作机会，尤其是在你有联系人的公司，从而增加面试机会。具体步骤包括：  
1. 获取联系人数据：从专业网络平台导出或自行创建CSV文件，包含姓名、公司、职位等信息。  
2. 试用样本数据：若无个人数据，可使用平台提供的样本CSV体验功能。  
3. 上传数据：上传ZIP档案或CSV文件以开始使用。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：LinkedIn的“人脉网络”筛选功能及其相关问题，包括隐私、数据使用和功能实现。

不同观点：
• 支持与认可：
  - [hackernewds] 认为这是一个LinkedIn本应该自己开发的完美功能，并对该功能表示感谢。
  - [shados] 强调AI将彻底改变整个行业，并指出这种功能可以快速构建，展示了技术进步对产品开发流程的冲击。

• 功能已经存在：
  - [floutist44] 指出该功能已经存在多年，用户可以通过在搜索查询中输入“in my network”实现同样的筛选效果。

• 隐私与数据安全担忧：
  - [thih9] 关注个人数据的上传和使用，询问是否存在隐私政策以及数据是否被存储或用于其他目的。
  - [bsoles] 提到下载和上传整个LinkedIn数据的要求，并指出数据包括连接、验证、联系人、账户历史等敏感信息。
  - [toyg] 对数据抓取和用户隐私表示担忧，建议使用官方API，并指出GDPR合规性的重要性。

• 实际应用与局限：
  - [1970-01-01] 提到有些人不使用LinkedIn但保留个人资料以维护声誉，质疑该功能的实际效果。
  - [b8] 分享个人经验，指出LinkedIn上大多数人只会接受陌生人的连接请求，但很少会提供推荐。

• 功能扩展建议：
  - [Fuzzy1000] 建议增加一个可以精确定位连接地点和方式的叠加功能。
  - [orliesaurus] 将该功能与Blind进行比较，认为其功能更为强大。
  - [dijit] 提出希望实现该功能的反向操作，即推荐曾经合作过的优秀人才，并讨论了实现此功能的复杂性和潜在问题。

补充讨论：
- 用户对LinkedIn功能实现的技术细节和隐私合规性有较多关注，特别是在涉及个人数据和GDPR合规性方面。
- 讨论中还涉及对AI技术和产品开发流程的思考，展示了技术进步如何改变传统产品开发周期。
- 部分用户对功能的真实需求和使用效果持怀疑态度，强调实际应用中的局限性。

Find jobs in your professional network
JobsByReferral analyzes your professional network to find job openings at companies where you have connections. Get referred by people you already know and dramatically increase your chances of landing interviews.
What's it look like?
1
Get your connections data
You can request a data archive from your professional network provider if you have one, or prepare a CSV file with your connections in the following format:
First Name, Last Name, URL, Email Address, Company, Position, Connected On
John, Smith, https://example.com/profile, john@email.com, Google, Software Engineer, 15 Jan 2024
Required fields:
First Name, Last Name, Company, Position
Optional fields:
URL, Email Address, Connected On
2
Want to try it with a sample export?
Don't have your professional network data yet? Try with our sample dataset to see how it works.
Download sample CSV
3
Ready to go with your data?
Upload either your professional network archive ZIP file, the extracted Connections.csv file, or the demo CSV to get started.
Upload your network data

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：冰泡作为数据存储媒介的可行性与相关联想

不同观点：
• **dtgriscom**：认为冰泡作为存储媒介不耐久，不是因为气候变化，而是由于表面能的作用。不同物质之间的边界会随着时间最小化，冰泡最终会变成球体，导致数据无法长期保存。他引用了自己在MIT学到的知识来支持这一观点。
  
• **meindnoch**：提出了一种更有创意的方法，即通过控制树木的年轮来存储信息。每一年可以用覆盖或不覆盖树来分别代表0或1。虽然存储速度很慢（1bit/年），但这一方法引发了对另类存储方式的讨论。

• **0xbadcafebee**：对冰媒介的长期保存性表示怀疑，语气较为调侃。

• **sprior**：将冰泡存储与亚马逊的存储服务类比，戏称为"Amazon Glacier"，带有调侃意味。

• **drfuchs**：通过历史类比，提到1979年的"Intel Magnetics 7110"磁泡存储芯片，暗示冰泡存储可能像过去的技术一样不实用。他还提到了对未来memristor技术的期待。

• **baruchel**：联想到文学作品中"冻结的词语"的概念，提供了文化和文学上的视角。

• **speedylight**：以幽默的方式提到用加热的方式来删除文件，暗示冰泡存储在实际操作中的不便。

• **hnanon12341**：仅仅对文章中的抽象图片表示赞赏，没有深入讨论存储技术本身。

• **lmpdev**：调侃文章本身像是在争取Ig Nobel Prize（搞笑诺贝尔奖），暗示其研究可能不切实际。

• **lloydatkinson**：提到如果要在1925年创建一个冰泡信息并在2025年读取，那么时间旅行是必要的，质疑了实际应用的可能性。

• **Mistletoe**：认为冰泡存储媒介虽然有趣，但实际使用效果可能很差。

• **AlienRobot**：以幽默的方式提到冰泡存储可能在核冬天后会有用，暗示极端环境下的潜在应用。

• **dzink**：对冰泡存储的想法来源表示好奇，但没有深入讨论技术细节。

• **moralestapia**：幽默地表示期待AWS版本的冰泡存储服务，将现代云服务与古老的存储概念结合。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于冰泡作为存储媒介的耐久性和实用性，特别是表面能对冰泡形状的影响。
• 讨论中多次出现幽默和调侃，反映了社区对这一概念实际可行性的普遍怀疑。
• 类比和历史技术（如磁泡存储芯片）的引用丰富了讨论，提供了更多视角。
• 部分评论引入了文化和文学联想，扩展了讨论的范围。

不同观点：
• **dtgriscom**：认为冰泡作为存储媒介不耐久，不是因为气候变化，而是由于表面能的作用。不同物质之间的边界会随着时间最小化，冰泡最终会变成球体，导致数据无法长期保存。他引用了自己在MIT学到的知识来支持这一观点。
  
• **meindnoch**：提出了一种更有创意的方法，即通过控制树木的年轮来存储信息。每一年可以用覆盖或不覆盖树来分别代表0或1。虽然存储速度很慢（1bit/年），但这一方法引发了对另类存储方式的讨论。

• **0xbadcafebee**：对冰媒介的长期保存性表示怀疑，语气较为调侃。

• **sprior**：将冰泡存储与亚马逊的存储服务类比，戏称为"Amazon Glacier"，带有调侃意味。

• **drfuchs**：通过历史类比，提到1979年的"Intel Magnetics 7110"磁泡存储芯片，暗示冰泡存储可能像过去的技术一样不实用。他还提到了对未来memristor技术的期待。

• **baruchel**：联想到文学作品中"冻结的词语"的概念，提供了文化和文学上的视角。

• **speedylight**：以幽默的方式提到用加热的方式来删除文件，暗示冰泡存储在实际操作中的不便。

• **hnanon12341**：仅仅对文章中的抽象图片表示赞赏，没有深入讨论存储技术本身。

• **lmpdev**：调侃文章本身像是在争取Ig Nobel Prize（搞笑诺贝尔奖），暗示其研究可能不切实际。

• **lloydatkinson**：提到如果要在1925年创建一个冰泡信息并在2025年读取，那么时间旅行是必要的，质疑了实际应用的可能性。

• **Mistletoe**：认为冰泡存储媒介虽然有趣，但实际使用效果可能很差。

• **AlienRobot**：以幽默的方式提到冰泡存储可能在核冬天后会有用，暗示极端环境下的潜在应用。

• **dzink**：对冰泡存储的想法来源表示好奇，但没有深入讨论技术细节。

• **moralestapia**：幽默地表示期待AWS版本的冰泡存储服务，将现代云服务与古老的存储概念结合。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于冰泡作为存储媒介的耐久性和实用性，特别是表面能对冰泡形状的影响。
• 讨论中多次出现幽默和调侃，反映了社区对这一概念实际可行性的普遍怀疑。
• 类比和历史技术（如磁泡存储芯片）的引用丰富了讨论，提供了更多视角。
• 部分评论引入了文化和文学联想，扩展了讨论的范围。

主要讨论点：二氧化碳捕集与封存的有效性和可行性

不同观点：
• [vjvjvjvjghv] 认为现有的二氧化碳捕集方法在规模上无法真正对气候变化产生显著影响，因为这些方法需要大量的能源、机械或空间。
• [briandw] 引用了关于使用核爆炸进行大规模碳捕集的研究，并对加速风化的方法表示支持和兴趣，认为这是一个有前景的方向。
• [verisimi] 对通过在船上携带石料来解决二氧化碳问题的方案表示怀疑，认为这不切实际，像是个糟糕的笑话。
• [tocs3] 提出船运的方案虽然能减少二氧化碳排放，但并不能实现负排放，并建议利用旧船通过太阳能和风能进行碳捕集。
• [trhway] 对在船上进行碳捕集的逻辑提出质疑，认为需要考虑石料粉碎、运输等过程中的碳排放，并建议改造旧船以实现半自主运行。
• [moralestapia] 认为许多碳捕集技术在计算“收益”时往往忽略了系统输入所带来的碳排放，例如石料粉碎、运输和燃料补偿等，最终可能导致排放更多碳，并强调无法违背热力学第二定律。
• [comrade1234] 以幽默方式评论，认为如果在船上放几桶酒可能会更好。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于碳捕集技术的实际可行性和规模化能力，尤其是考虑整个过程中隐含的碳排放。
• 讨论中多次提到船运方案的实际操作和潜在问题，包括能源消耗和效率影响。
• [moralestapia] 的评论指出碳捕集技术的理想化模型与现实中碳排放之间的矛盾，强调了系统性考虑的重要性。
• [briandw] 对新技术研究表示乐观，但其他评论者多持怀疑态度。

data.title: You are what you launch: how software became a lifestyle brand
data.author: freediver
data.article_summary: 这篇文章探讨了软件如何从单纯的工具演变为个人身份和品味的象征。过去选择软件只需看其功能是否满足需求，而现在，像Notion或Obsidian这样的软件更像是一种生活方式的表达，反映出用户的个性与部落归属感。Notion以简洁、模块化的设计和高度可定制性成为一种审美工作空间，适合追求美感与秩序的人。而Obsidian则以功能性和探索性吸引那些喜欢深入研究和技术操作的用户。两者不仅吸引了不同类型的用户，更代表了不同的生活态度：一个注重美学和协作，另一个则强调功能性和私密性。软件不再只是工具，而是一种无声的自我表达和身份构建。

44432055.article_content:
you are what you launch: how software became a lifestyle brand
01 Apr, 2025
software used to be functional. now it’s personal. this is an essay about tools, taste, and the quiet ways we curate identity through what we launch.
intro
choosing software used to be straightforward. does the app do what you need, or not? but now, opening notion or obsidian feels less like launching software and more like putting on your favorite jacket. it says something about you. aligns you with a tribe, becomes part of your identity. software isn’t just functional anymore. it’s quietly turned into a lifestyle brand, a digital prosthetic we use to signal who we are, or who we wish we were.
there’s been a shift. not dramatic, but gradual. slow. quiet. like how one day you realize everyone around you stopped using chrome. somewhere along the way, software stopped being invisible. it started meaning things. your browser, your calendar, your to-do list, these are not just tools anymore. they are taste. alignment. self-expression.
suddenly your app stack said something about you. not in a loud, obvious way but like the kind of shoes you wear when you don’t want people to notice, but still want them to
know
. margiela replica. new balance 992. arcteryx. stuff that whispers instead of shouts, it’s all about signaling to the right people. you don’t want everyone to notice, just the ones whose opinion actually matter to you. maybe this isn’t an essay about software at all. maybe it’s about taste as self-construction. or function as aesthetic.
notion: the aesthetic workspace
staying with the fashion metaphor for a bit, our apps are like our outfits, our docks are our fit pics. curated, intentional, meant to be seen. maybe not by everyone, but by
someone
. that’s what made
dockhunt
so fascinating when it blew up like 2 years ago on twitter. it turned utility into exhibition, something private into a public moodboard. you weren’t just sharing what you use, you were showing who you are.
and what did we see when the docks came out?
arc
over chrome and safari.
notion
over notes and reminders. tools with personalities, tools that signaled intention.
and no tool owns that space better than notion. it’s not just a notes app, it’s a whole aesthetic.
calm, blank, modular.
the kind of calm that feels curated. everything’s clean, but not sterile. soft fonts, careful spacing, subtle off-white coloring, the tasteful thickness…
notion might be one of the most unopinionated tools out there. you can build practically anything with it. databases, journals, dashboards, even websites. but for a tool so open-ended, it’s surprisingly curated. only three fonts, ten colors. it’s like apple before they started chasing android. there was a time when iOS felt like intentional restraint. now, with iOS 18 letting you recolor every icon to match your wallpaper, i’ve seen home screens so hideous that i’d never associate them with apple at all.
this kind of restraint doesn’t happen by accident. it’s a mindset. a way of treating software like craft. the paint, the jackets, the “couldn’t find merch we love”. this is literally vibe-maxxing as company ethos. it shows how deeply they aestheticize every layer of the brand. they’re not just building a tool, they’re building a taste. a tone.
and it shows. the app reflects the company. or maybe the company reflects the app. either way, the branding isn’t loud. it’s soft-spoken and super curated. like who else
talks
about paint swatches and jackets when hitting 100 million users?
obsidian: the tinkerer’s lab
and then there’s
obsidian
.
same category. completely different energy.
if notion is a sleek apartment in seoul, obsidian is a cluttered home lab. markdown files. local folders. keyboard shortcuts. graph views. it doesn’t care how it looks, it cares that it works. it’s functional first, aesthetic maybe never. there’s no onboarding flow, no emoji illustrations, no soft gradients telling you everything’s going to be okay. just an empty vault and the quiet suggestion: you figure it out.
obsidian is built for
tinkerers
. not in the modern, drag and drop sense but in the old way. the “i wanna see how this thing works under the hood way”. it’s a tool that rewards curiosity and exploration. everything in obsidian feels like it was made by someone who didn’t just want to take notes, they wanted to build the system that takes notes. it’s messy, it’s endless, and that’s the point. it’s a playground for people who believe that the best tools are the ones you shape yourself.
notion is for people who want a beautiful space to live in, obsidian is for people who want to wire the whole building from scratch. both offer freedom, but one is curated and the other is raw.
obsidian and notion don’t just attract different users.
they attract different lifestyles.
simulacra of openness
notion is collaborative, aesthetic, made to be shared. it leans soft. social.
obsidian is solitary recursive, private. it leans hard. technical.
one rewards presen

data.title: Ubuntu 25.10 Raises RISC-V Profile Requirements
data.author: bundie
data.article_summary: Canonical计划在Ubuntu 25.10中提升对RISC-V设备的支持，但大多数现有RISC-V设备将无法运行该版本。这是因为Ubuntu 25.10将基准RISC-V配置文件（RVA）从RVA20升级到RVA23，后者要求强制支持向量和虚拟化扩展，以满足更高性能需求如AI、加密和企业工作负载。现有设备如Orange Pi RV2由于缺乏这些扩展将无法支持新版本。不过，Ubuntu 24.04 LTS仍将支持到2029年，因此短期内影响不大。长期来看，这一升级将有助于Ubuntu在RISC-V平台上占据主导地位，但目前支持RVA23的设备还很少。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Ubuntu及相关操作系统对RISC-V等新硬件架构的支持策略及其争议

不同观点：
• [shirro] 认为操作系统在技术快速发展的背景下做出支持新硬件的决定非常困难。以RISC-V为例，虽然当前选择支持更高规格的硬件可能是明智的，但如果较低规格的RISC-V突然流行起来，可能会错失机会。他以Debian为例，指出Debian曾将32位ARM硬浮点系统的最低目标设为armv7，但后来由于Raspberry Pi（基于armv6）的流行，用户遇到了问题，最后通过Raspbian解决了这个问题。

• [johnklos] 对Ubuntu的硬件支持策略持批评态度，认为Ubuntu对“低端”系统的支持不足，并讽刺其对未来硬件的支持过于超前，甚至支持了一些尚未存在的硬件（如RVA23设备），可能导致用户转向其他操作系统。他还提到，如果Ubuntu继续这样定位，可能会失去用户。

• [somanyphotons] 认为RVA23是一个对Linux机器长期有益的指令集架构（ISA），并推测Ubuntu可能提前知晓了一些即将发布的硬件。他还提出了RVA23是否与RISC-V上的Android需求一致的问题。

• [csense] 提出了一种技术解决方案，询问是否可以通过内核补丁或驱动程序来捕获不支持的指令，并用软件实现这些指令。

• [Levitating] 表示希望有一些Ubuntu提前知晓但尚未公布的硬件。

• [fithisux] 指出目前市场上还没有消费者可用的RV23 mini-ITX、micro-ATX或ATX规格的设备，并提到Orange PI 2存在图形blob问题。

• [throwaway48476] 认为RISC-V应用处理器标准中的缺失部分逐渐补全过程中，类似的问题会不断出现。

• [delfinom] 批评Canonical（Ubuntu的开发公司）试图再次分化市场，暗示其试图通过支持特定硬件来主导某个领域。

补充讨论：
- 讨论中多次提到RISC-V硬件支持的现状及其不确定性，尤其是RVA23设备在市场上的缺乏。
- 有人对Ubuntu过于超前的硬件支持策略表示不满，认为可能导致用户流失。
- 也有一些技术性讨论，如通过软件实现来解决硬件支持问题。
- Debian的历史案例被用来对比当前Ubuntu面临的类似困境。
- Canonical的市场策略受到质疑，被认为是在分化市场。

A recent bug report filed against Ubuntu’s upgrading tool confirmed a major change with regards to the RISC-V requirements for the upcoming Ubuntu 25.10 release — most existing RISC-V devices will
not
be able to run Ubuntu 25.10.
How come?
A New Baseline for RISC-V
Ubuntu 25.10 plans to bumps its baseline RISC-V profile (RVA) from RVA20 to RVA23. It may sound like a small jump but it has a big impact since the bulk of RISC-V devices currently sold don’t support it.
An RVA (RISC-V Application) profile is a specification that outlines the vector processing capabilities a RISC-V system must have, so
“software can rely on the existence of a certain set of […] features in a particular generation of RISC-V implementations”.
That’s according to RISC-V International, the main collaborative group steering and overseeing development of this open source and royalty free processor architecture.
“RISC-V was designed to provide a highly modular and extensible instruction set (ISA) and includes a large and growing set of standard extensions, where each standard extension is a bundle of instruction-set features,”
RISC-V International explains.
The
RVA23 profile
makes a number of ‘extensions’ mandatory, notably
Vector and Hypervisor extensions
to power
“math-intensive workloads including AI/ML & cryptography, and enterprise hardware, operating systems and software workloads
.”
Per Samsung
, the RISC-V ‘V’ Vector extension
“allows CPUs to perform many operations simultaneously, making them faster and more efficient”
. With RVA23 RISC-V reaches a clear feature parity level with ARMv9 and x86-64v4.
It is (naturally) more involved than that. Plenty of
deep-dives on RISC-V Vector extensions
are available online if you find yourself curious about the computational underpinnings and future opportunities they stand to provide.
Impact on Existing Hardware
According to an open issue on Launchpad
, the
“ubuntu-release-upgrader should stop upgrades beyond Ubuntu 24.04 on hardware that does not support the RVA23U64 profile”
, noting that
“RVA23U64 is the profile relevant for user space”
.
Support for earlier versions of Ubuntu on existing RISC-V hadn’t isn’t impacted, but this change does mean that Ubuntu 25.10 (and later) will not run on
most
existing RISC-V hardware (like the
Orange Pi RV2
) since they lack the extensions the RVA23 profile requires.
Will that really be an issue long-term?
Ubuntu 24.04 LTS is supported until 2029 at the earliest and will continue to work on existing hardware, so that’s covered. RISC-V usage remains niche so the impact from Ubuntu ‘raising the bar’ on baseline  profile requirements won’t be huge.
What could be huge is the benefit to Ubuntu going forward.
Focusing future Ubuntu support to devices that have more capable RISC-V profile sets will further position the distro as the
de-facto
OS on the platform. As workload demands increase, and RISC-V hardware becomes more capable and affordable, the opportunities are obvious.
Admittedly there is one big rub: the range of RISC-V devices with RVA23 support is, at the time or writing this, near non-existent. That will change in the coming year, and by the release of Ubuntu 26.04 LTS, the distro will be primed to take full advantage.
RISC-V
Ubuntu 25.10
44431828.article_summary: Canonical计划在Ubuntu 25.10中提升对RISC-V设备的支持，但大多数现有RISC-V设备将无法运行该版本。这是因为Ubuntu 25.10将基准RISC-V配置文件（RVA）从RVA20升级到RVA23，后者要求强制支持向量和虚拟化扩展，以满足更高性能需求如AI、加密和企业工作负载。现有设备如Orange Pi RV2由于缺乏这些扩展将无法支持新版本。不过，Ubuntu 24.04 LTS仍将支持到2029年，因此短期内影响不大。长期来看，这一升级将有助于Ubuntu在RISC-V平台上占据主导地位，但目前支持RVA23的设备还很少。

主要讨论点：用户对一款名为Jupad的笔记计算工具的功能、使用体验及技术细节的讨论。

不同观点：
• [idanp] 介绍了Jupad工具，并提供了一个概念验证（POC）链接，强调了其使用Python的特点。
• [johncosta27] 对工具的实用性表示赞赏，特别提到其在预算计算方面的便捷性，介于纸笔和完整电子表格之间。
• [zuzzurro] 提出了单位转换和计算中的问题，指出在使用不同时间单位时结果不符合预期，需要转换为秒来计算。
• [xz18r] 推荐了另一款基于mathjs的工具Numerals，强调其在Obsidian中的良好表现和自动求和功能。
• [shepik] 对工具的界面表示赞赏，但指出单位处理中的异常，如"150 kn to km/h"被误认为减法而非转换。
• [zamadatix] 对工具的交互和语法表示赞赏，但对CRDT在同步中的使用提出疑问，担心同步冲突问题。
• [abfar] 指出了计算优先级的问题，例如除法在幂运算前执行，结果与预期不符。
• [kragen] 对工具的UI流程表示赞赏，但关心其代码许可问题，担心版权风险。
• [eviks] 提到工具不支持上标显示，并询问CRDT是否可用于丰富的撤销历史功能，而非仅限于同步。
• [ajjenkins] 对工具的创意和执行表示赞赏，但不确定其实际用途。
• [wslh] 提到寻找其他笔记计算工具时发现了奇怪的产品，提供了一个链接。

补充讨论：
• 用户对工具的单位转换功能有较多讨论，尤其是对结果不符合预期的具体例子进行了详细描述。
• 用户对CRDT技术在工具中的应用表示关注，主要集中在同步冲突和多用户编辑场景下的使用。
• 对计算优先级的疑问反映了用户对数学运算顺序的期望，特别是在不同运算符混合使用时的执行顺序。
• 代码许可和版权问题也被提及，反映了用户在选择工具时对法律风险的关注。

data.title: FossFLOW: Make beautiful isometric infrastructure diagrams
data.author: nateb2022
data.article_summary: FossFLOW是一个开源的渐进式网页应用（PWA），用于创建精美的等距基础设施图。它使用React和Isoflow库构建，完全运行于浏览器中，支持离线使用。主要功能包括自动保存、导入/导出图表、隐私优先（数据存储在本地浏览器中）、以及PWA支持，可在Mac和Linux上作为原生应用安装。用户可以通过拖放组件、连接关系、自定义颜色和标签等方式创建图表，并能管理多个保存的图表。部署时，需注意PWA功能需要HTTPS支持，图表存储在浏览器localStorage中，有5-10MB的限制。项目欢迎贡献，采用Unlicense许可协议。

• [dddw] 对工具表示了简单的认可，并表示愿意尝试，没有提出具体的技术需求或功能要求，态度较为中立和积极。

FossFLOW - Isometric Diagramming Tool
FossFLOW is a powerful, open-source Progressive Web App (PWA) for creating beautiful isometric diagrams. Built with React and the Isoflow (Now forked and published to NPM as fossflow) library, it runs entirely in your browser with offline support.
📝
FOSSFLOW_TODO.md
- Current issues and roadmap with codebase mappings, most gripes are with the isoflow library itself.
🤝
CONTRIBUTORS.md
- How to contribute to the project.
Features
🎨
Isometric Diagramming
- Create stunning 3D-style technical diagrams
💾
Auto-Save
- Your work is automatically saved every 5 seconds
📱
PWA Support
- Install as a native app on Mac and Linux
🔒
Privacy-First
- All data stored locally in your browser
📤
Import/Export
- Share diagrams as JSON files
🎯
Session Storage
- Quick save without dialogs
🌐
Offline Support
- Work without internet connection
Quick Start
#
Clone the repository
git clone https://github.com/stan-smith/FossFLOW
cd
FossFLOW
#
Make sure you have npm installed
#
Install dependencies
npm install
#
Start development server
npm start
Open
http://localhost:3000
in your browser.
How to Use
Creating Diagrams
Add Items
: Drag and drop components from the library onto the canvas
Connect Items
: Use connectors to show relationships between components
Customize
: Change colors, labels, and properties of items
Navigate
: Pan and zoom to work on different areas
Saving Your Work
Auto-Save
: Diagrams are automatically saved to browser storage every 5 seconds
Quick Save
: Click "Quick Save (Session)" for instant saves without popups
Save As
: Use "Save New" to create a copy with a different name
Managing Diagrams
Load
: Click "Load" to see all your saved diagrams
Import
: Load diagrams from JSON files shared by others
Export
: Download your diagrams as JSON files to share or backup
Storage
: Use "Storage Manager" to manage browser storage space
Keyboard Shortcuts
Delete
- Remove selected items
Mouse wheel - Zoom in/out
Click and drag - Pan around canvas
NEW
Crtl+Z undo Ctrl+Y redo
Building for Production
#
Create optimized production build
npm run build
#
Serve the production build locally

data.title: Kyutai 1.6B Streaming TTS
data.author: robotswantdata
data.article_summary: Kyutai TTS 是一个用于流式文本到语音（TTS）生成的模型，能够在输入文本的初始部分后立即输出音频。该模型采用分层Transformer架构，通过Mimi标记化音频，帧率为12.5 Hz，音频帧由32个音频标记表示。模型包含10亿参数，支持英语和法语，并通过预计算嵌入进行语音条件设置。训练历时75万步，使用250万小时的公开音频内容，并在32个Nvidia H100 GPU上进行预训练。该模型不支持分类自由引导（CFG）和水印，但通过预计算语音嵌入限制语音克隆能力。

44458858.article_content:
Model Card for Kyutai TTS
See also the
project page
,
the
Colab example
,
and the
GitHub repository
. Pre-print research paper is coming soon!
This is a model for streaming text-to-speech (TTS).
Unlike offline text-to-speech, where the model needs the entire text to produce the audio,
our model starts to output audio as soon as the first few words from the text have been given as input.
Model Details
The model architecture is a hierarchical Transformer that consumes tokenized text and generateds audio tokenized by Mimi,
see
the Moshi paper
.
The frame rate is 12.5 Hz and each audio frame is represented by 32 audio tokens, although you can use less tokens at inference time for faster generation.
The backbone model is 1B parameters, and the depth transformer is 600M parameters and uses partial weight sharing similar to
Hibiki
.
The audio is shifted by 16 steps (1.28 sec.) with respect to the text, and the model uses an acoustic/semantic delay of 2.
Model Description
Kyutai TTS is a decoder-only model for streaming speech-to-text.
It leverages the multistream architecture of
Moshi
to model text stream based on the speech stream.
The text stream is shifted w.r.t. the audio stream to allow the model to predict text tokens based on the input audio.
Developed by: Kyutai
Model type: Streaming Text-To-Speech.
Language(s) (NLP): English and French
License: Model weights are licensed under CC-BY 4.0
Repository:
GitHub
Uses
Direct Use
This model is able to perform streaming text-to-speech generation, including dialogs.
The model supports voice conditioning through cross-attention pre-computed embeddings,
which are provided for a number of voices in our
tts-voices
repository.
This model does not support Classifier Free Guidance (CFG) directly, but was trained with
CFG distillation
for improved speed (no need to double the batch size).
It is easy to batch and can reach a throughput of 75x generated audio per compute unit of time.
This model does not perform watermarking for two reasons:
watermarking can easily be deactivated for open source models,
our early experiments show that all watermark systems used by existing TTS are removed by simply encodeding and decoding the audio with Mimi.
Instead, we prefered to restrict the voice cloning ability to the use of pre-computed voice embeddings.
How to Get Started with the Model
See the
GitHub repository
.
Training Details
The model was trained for 750k steps, with a batch size of 64, and a segment duration of 120 seconds. Then, CFG distillation was performed for 24k updates.
Training Data
Pretraining stage: we use an audio collection of 2.5 million hours of publicly available audio content.
For this dataset, we obtained synthetic transcripts by running
whisper-timestamped
with
whisper-medium
.
Compute Infrastructure
Pretraining was done with 32 H100 Nvidia GPUs. CFG distillation was done on 8 such GPUs.
Model Card Authors
Neil Zeghidour, Eugene Kharitonov, Manu Orsini, Václav Volhejn, Gabriel de Marmiesse, Edouard Grave, Patrick Perez, Laurent Mazaré, Alexandre Défossez

data.title: ASCIIMoon: The moon's phase live in ASCII art
data.author: zayat
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了一个通过ASCII艺术展示月亮每日相位变化的工具。用户可以查看并循环浏览不同日期的月亮相位，界面以ASCII字符构成月亮图案。页面包含日期选择功能，用户可以点击"前一天"或"后一天"来查看不同日期的月亮相位图。图案以各种符号模拟月亮的不同形态，如新月、上弦月、满月和下弦月等。这个工具提供了一种直观且艺术化的方式来观察月相变化。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：ASCII艺术 moon phase 表示的准确性与艺术性

不同观点：
• **SlowTao 的观点**：喜欢ASCII艺术，但指出月相的呈现不准确，特别是在半月时应精确显示一半被遮挡，而不是一个奇怪的圆形缺口。同时提到在《GTA San Andreas》中也见过类似处理，但由于当时技术限制可以理解。建议对阴影进行调整以提升效果。

• **thot_experiment 的观点**：认为ASCII艺术在非标准文本模式下会失去一些魅力，尤其是当其大小和颜色变化不符合传统终端显示时。自认可能是个“纯粹主义者”。

• **_aavaa 的观点**：认为使用位图作为圆形和阴影的遮罩是取巧的做法，缺乏真正的ASCII艺术精神。

• **angry_albatross 的观点**：指出该项目声称“以ASCII艺术渲染”具有误导性，因为月相的呈现实际上并不是ASCII文本的一部分。同时附和其他人对月相显示不准确的批评。

• **shagie 的观点**：引用项目关于页面的说明，强调这是一个个人项目，不追求精确性。但通过数学计算指出当前月相的照明比例不正确，建议进行修正以提高准确性。

• **p1mrx 的观点**：认为当前的阴影呈现看起来物理上不可能，除非是在月食期间。不过，至少没有在阴影中加入星星，还算给了“部分分数”。

• **jpecar 的观点**：回忆起ACME phoon项目，提到曾将其加入自己的.bashrc中，暗示对ASCII艺术表现形式的怀旧和认可。

• **spicybright 的观点**：批评CSS动画在呈现月相变化时显得不够流畅，视觉效果不佳。

• **tingletech 的观点**：分享了自己用JavaScript和SVG制作月相的项目，暗示对技术实现的不同看法。

• **Nition 的观点**：认为项目效果不错，但指出月相的呈现有误，特别是在南半球用户的角度应进行180度旋转以符合实际情况。同时指出精确度与实现难度之间的平衡问题。

• **lifthrasiir 的观点**：提到其他类似ASCII艺术实现的资源和项目，如IOCCC获奖作品，暗示对当前项目技术实现的不同看法。

• **tolerance 的观点**：认为对天文准确性的批评是合理的，但同时也呼吁关注ASCII艺术的“艺术”价值，认为项目看起来很酷，实现不易，且颜色变化增加了趣味性。

• **layer8 的观点**：指出在桌面浏览器上放大过多时，ASCII部分和剪裁圆的匹配会出问题。同时提到在足够高的字符“分辨率”下，ASCII艺术可以接近像素艺术，并给出了具体字符大小和终端显示的建议。

• **D___R___ 的观点**：回忆起童年在天文馆购买月球土地的经历，认为该项目带有类似的怀旧和数字化的魅力。

• **JKCalhoun 的观点**：认为项目很酷，但希望阴影能更符合现实，特别是新月形状应通过南北极并随着接近四分之一月而变平。

补充讨论：
- 争议焦点在于ASCII艺术呈现的准确性与艺术性之间的平衡。
- 天文准确性是多数评论者关注的重点，但也有评论者强调项目的艺术价值和技术实现的难度。
- 不同评论者提供了其他类似项目的参考和个人经验分享，丰富了讨论内容。

• 讨论中体现了技术实现与用户体验之间的张力，npinsker强调用户体验和“核心幻想”的重要性，而其他评论者更关注技术选型和数据处理等后台问题。

data.author: jnord
data.article_summary: 文章主要介绍物理学家在密歇根州立大学的稀有同位素束流设施（FRIB）通过实验揭示重元素（如金、铅、钡等）如何在恒星中形成。FRIB实验室通过加速原子核并使其撞击目标来模拟恒星内部的条件，重现重元素形成的过程，特别是所谓的“中子捕获过程”。这一研究帮助科学家理解比铁更重的元素是如何在宇宙中生成的。实验室目前专注于模拟三种主要过程之一，即“中间中子捕获过程”（i-process），并计划模拟产生如铂和金等“珠宝店元素”的过程。这一研究标志着在理解重元素形成方面取得了重大进展。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于破碎盘子的类比是否恰当，以及在科学实验中获取特定同位素的难度比较。

不同观点：
• [观点1 - 类比的有效性] ordu认为将破碎盘子的类比用于解释核物理中的i过程和r过程可能不够准确。他质疑较小的碎片是否真的更难获得，因为较小的碎片应该包含较少的细节，理论上应该更容易找到。按照他的逻辑，较大的碎片需要保留更多的细节，因此找到特定碎片的概率应该更低。
  
• [观点2 - 类比的科学背景] 类比是由核 astrophysicist Hendrik Schatz 提出的，他将寻找特定同位素的过程比作从破碎的盘子中找到特定图案。他认为，由于实验中产生的大量碎片（每秒上万亿个），找到特定同位素就像从大量碎片中找到极少数符合要求的碎片一样困难。这一类比旨在强调实验中筛选和识别特定同位素的难度。

补充讨论：
• [类比的局限性] ordu指出了类比的可能局限，即在物理上，较小的碎片在某些情况下可能比大碎片更容易获取和识别，因为其复杂性较低。然而，在核物理实验中，由于涉及的原子和同位素的性质，即便是较小的碎片也可能极难分离和识别。

• [争议焦点] 争议的焦点在于类比是否能准确反映实验中寻找特定同位素的实际难度。ordu质疑类比是否过度简化了科学过程，而Schatz的类比则更倾向于形象化解释复杂的过程，以便让非专业人士更容易理解。

Physicists Start To Pin Down How Stars Forge Heavy Atoms
By
Jenna Ahart
July 2, 2025
The precursors of heavy elements might arise in the plasma underbellies of swollen stars or in smoldering stellar corpses. They definitely exist in East Lansing, Michigan.
Comment
Save Article

Experiments in Michigan are unraveling how elements heavier than iron are made.
Mark Belan/
Quanta Magazine
Introduction
By
Jenna Ahart
Contributing Writer
July 2, 2025
View PDF/Print Mode
astronomy
astrophysics
neutron stars
nuclear physics
physics

The Facility for Rare Isotope Beams (FRIB) may not glitter quite like the night sky, plunked as it is between Michigan State University’s chemistry department and the performing arts center. Inside, though, the lab is teeming with substances that are otherwise found only in stars.
Here, atomic nuclei accelerate to half the speed of light, smash into a target and shatter into smithereens. The collisions create some of the same rare, unstable isotopes that arise inside stars and which, through a sequence of further reactions, end up as heavy elements.
FRIB scientists have been re-creating the recipe.
“People like to do DNA tests to see where their ancestors came from,” said
Artemis Spyrou
, a nuclear astrophysicist at FRIB. “We’re doing the same with our planet and solar system.”
Scientists have a solid understanding of how stars forge the elements on the periodic table up to iron. But the processes that give rise to heavier elements — zinc, lead, barium, gold and the rest — are more elusive.
Now, tangible results have emerged in a field replete with postulates and presumptions. The FRIB lab is currently replicating one of the three main processes by which heavy elements are thought to form, and homing in on where this “intermediate neutron-capture process,” or
i-
process, occurs.
The lab also plans to re-create one of the other two processes as well, the one that yields “jewelry shop elements” such as platinum and gold.
“This is a big, big jump forward in understanding how isotopes form. Then we can go backward and find the astrophysical sites with the right conditions,” said
John Cowan
, who first theorized about the
i-
process as a graduate student in the 1970s. “FRIB is doing some pioneering work.”
Building the Elements
Some 13.8 billion years ago, the newborn universe was a scorching soup of elementary particles, freshly forged in the Big Bang. As the cosmos cooled and expanded, these specks combined to form subatomic particles such as protons and neutrons, which combined to form hydrogen, helium and lithium — the first and lightest elements — during the universe’s first three minutes. It would take another couple hundred million years for these elements to clump together into larger bodies and birth stars.

Artemis Spyrou, a physicist at the Facility for Rare Isotope Beams (FRIB) and Michigan State University, poses with the Summing Nal (SuN) detector at FRIB, a gamma-ray detector used to measure decaying isotopes.
Courtesy of Facility for Rare Isotope Beams
Once stars lit up the cosmos, the universe grew chemically richer. In a star’s hot, dense core, atomic nuclei smash into each other with immense force, fusing to form new elements. When hydrogen nuclei (which have one proton apiece) fuse, they form helium; three of those fuse into carbon, and so on. This nuclear fusion releases heaps of energy that presses outward, preventing the star from collapsing under the pressure of its own gravity. As a massive star ages, it fuses increasingly heavy elements, moving up the periodic table. That is, until it gets to iron.
At that point, further fusion doesn’t release energy; it absorbs it. Without new energy from fusion, the star’s death becomes imminent. Its core contracts inward, and a shock wave blasts everything else outward — creating a supernova.
For everything past iron on the periodic table, a different origin story is needed.
In the 1950s, physicists
came up
with
one
: “neutron capture.” In this process, nuclei collect neutral, free-floating subatomic particles called neutrons. As these glom on, the nucleus becomes an unstable version of itself — a radioactive isotope. Balance is restored when its excess neutrons transform into positively charged protons in a process called beta decay. Gaining a proton turns the nucleus into the next element on the periodic table.
Mark Belan/
Quanta Magazine
To reach its final form, an atomic nucleus typically moves through a string of different radioactive isotopes, collecting more and more neutrons as it goes.

Germany
Unknown novel by writer who charted Hitler’s rise becomes German bestseller
Sebastian Haffner’s love story set in final days of Weimar Republic published more than nine decades after it was written
Kate Connolly
in Berlin
Tue 24 Jun 2025 00.00 EDT
Share
A previously unknown novel by one of Europe’s most influential postwar journalists which captures the heady yet fragile spirit of the final days of the Weimar Republic has been published in
Germany
after his children discovered the hand-written manuscript in his desk.
More than nine decades after he wrote it, Sebastian Haffner’s Abschied or Parting has soared to the
top of the Spiegel bestseller list
following its debut earlier this month.
Haffner, who fled Nazi Berlin with his Jewish fiancee in 1938, achieved instant recognition in 1940 with his penetrating prewar classic Germany: Jekyll and Hyde. Winston Churchill is said to have told his cabinet to read it in order to comprehend the Nazi threat.
The Jewish dealer who bought art hated by the Nazis – and created one of the greatest collections ever seen
Read more
Haffner, who changed his name in the UK from Raimund Pretzel in order to protect family still living in Germany, went on to work as a journalist in London for the Observer. He was recognised as one of the commanding analysts of nazism and what brought Hitler to power, returning to Berlin for the Observer in 1954, and later becoming a prominent columnist for the news magazine Stern.
His son, Oliver Pretzel, 86, said his family had deliberated for years over whether to release Parting after Haffner’s death
in Berlin aged 91
in 1999. They had been concerned, he said, that the work, a love story, might have seemed too slight, and overshadowed their father’s towering reputation as a heavyweight commentator.
“My sister didn’t think the novel was very good,” Pretzel, a professor of mathematics based in London, told the Süddeutsche Zeitung. “I initially shared this view somewhat. But when I re-read it and since I set about translating it into English, I suddenly realised how ingeniously constructed it is.”
Happily, the critics seem to agree. In Germany they have heaped praise on the 181-page work, calling it “a literary windfall”, an “incredibly fast-paced, light, and lively text”, and “a beautiful book of youthful sparkle and great emotional impact”.
View image in fullscreen
Haffner with Gertrude Joseph, on whom the main female character in the novel is based.
Photograph: Supplied
Set on the last day of a two-week sojourn in Paris by the protagonist and his love interest, Teddy, before he has to return to a Berlin overcome by a growing sense of fear and political uncertainty, the novel was “shockingly lucid”, Marie Schmidt wrote in the Süddeutsche.
The novel reflected the same “keen historical awareness that astonished and fascinated the world” in Haffner’s other posthumous work, History of a German, she added. That book was written in 1939 but only published for the first time in German in 2000, and in English, under the title Defying Hitler, in 2002. It was praised for its clear-sighted scrutiny and credited with extinguishing the repeated assertions of Haffner’s contemporaries that they had not known about Nazi crimes.
Jekyll and Hyde was first published in Germany in 1996 under the title:
1939 – Deutschland von
innen betrachtet
(Germany observed from within). Both books also topped the German bestseller lists when they were published.
Haffner was 24 when he wrote Parting in just a few weeks in October and November 1932, just months before the Nazis came to power. His attempts to get it published failed.
Its narrator, Raimund, is an apprentice lawyer who smokes Gitanes Rouge and reads Aldous Huxley. In Paris in the spring of 1931 he meets Teddy, who has left Berlin, describing it as a time in which “crisis had not yet been invented”.
Teddy is thought to have been based on Gertrude Joseph, a Jewish woman from Vienna with whom Haffner had been in love. He described in his autobiographical book History of a German how she had returned to Nazi Berlin from Paris for the last time in the summer of 1933, bringing with her “an air that one could breathe, and which one breathed in greedily”. Raimund in the novel describes the growing foreboding of having to “leave for a cold Berlin”.
Haffner and Joseph, who ended up in Sweden, kept in touch until the end of their days. Twenty letters from him to her were found in her possession on her death.
In an epilogue to the novel, the literary critic Volker Weidermann says the family’s fears about its publication were unfounded.

data.article_summary: 文章讨论了语言模型（LLMs）中的种族和性别偏见问题，特别是其思维链（Chain-of-Thought, CoT）推理的不忠实性。作者指出，当前模型在无特别干预下往往表现出“觉醒”倾向，偏向于非白人和非男性候选人。尽管实验室已努力解决此问题，但出于公关和政治气候考虑，公司可能不会急于改变这种偏见，甚至可能默许其存在以避免争议。文章还探讨了开发者在调整模型政治倾向时的动机和挑战，指出由于现实中的对齐难度，开发者可能倾向于让模型略微左倾，以避免更大的风险。总体而言，文章强调了模型偏见与开发者意图之间的复杂关系，以及在解决此类问题时的实际困难。

Hmm, I don't want to derail the comments on this post with a bunch of culture war things, but these two sentences in combination seemed to me to partially contradict each other:
When present, the bias is always against white and male candidates across all tested models and scenarios.
[...]
The problem (race and gender bias) is one that labs have spent a substantial amount of effort to address, which mimics realistic misalignment settings.
I agree that the labs have spent a substantial amount of effort to address this issue, but the current behavior seems in-line with the aims of the labs? Most of the pressure comes from left-leaning academics or reporters, who I think are largely in-favor of affirmative action. The world where the AI systems end up with a margin of safety to be biased against white male candidates, in order to reduce the likelihood they ever look like they discriminate in the other direction (which would actually be at substantial risk of blowing up), while not talking explicitly about the reasoning itself since that would of course prove highly controversial, seems basically the ideal result from a company PR perspective.
I don't currently think that is what's going on, but I do think due to these dynamics, the cited benefit of this scenario for studying the faithfulness of CoT reasoning seems currently not real to me. My guess is companies do not have a strong incentive to change this current behavior, and indeed I can't immediately think of a behavior in this domain the companies would prefer from a selfish perspective.

It's a bit tricky because it's hard to cite specific evidence here, so I'll just state my beliefs without trying to substantiate them much:
By default—i.e. when training models without special attention to their political orientations—I think frontier LLMs end up being pretty woke
[1]
.
There are lots of ways you can try to modify model's political orientations, not all of which map cleanly onto the left-right axis (e.g. trying to make models more generally open-minded). But if we were to naively map AI developers' interventions onto a left-right axis, I would guess that the large majority of these interventions would push in the "stop being so leftist" direction.
This is because (a) some companies (especially Google) have gotten a lot of flak for their AIs being really woke, (b) empirically I think that publicly available LLMs are less woke than they would be without interventions, and (c) the current political climate really doesn't look kindly on woke AI.
[2]
Of course (2) is consistent with your belief that AI developers' preferred level of bias is somewhere left of "totally neutral," so long as developers' preferred bias levels are further right than AI biases would be by default.
I'm not very confident about this, but I'd weakly guess that if AI developers were good at hitting alignment targets, they would actually prefer for their AIs to be politically neutral. Given that developers likely expect to miss what they're aiming for, I think it's plausible that they'd rather miss in a left-leaning direction, meaning that they'd overall aim for slightly left-leaning AIs. But again, I'm not confident here and I find it plausible (~10% likely) that these days they'd overall aim for slightly right-leaning AIs.
TBC it's possible I'm totally wrong about all this stuff, and no one should cite this comment as giving strong evidence about what Anthropic does. In particular, I was surprised that Rohin Shah—who I expect would know better than I would about common AI developer practices—reacted "disagree" to the claim that "The problem (race and gender bias) is one that labs have spent a substantial amount of effort to address."
^
This is mostly an empirical observation, but I think a plausible mechanism might be something like: Educated people on the internet tend to be left-leaning, so when you train the model to write like an educated person, it also ends up inheriting left-leaning views.
^
It's not clear how directly influential these media outlets are, but it might be interesting to read the right-wing coverage of our paper (
Daily Wire
,
Washington Examiner
).

data.title: Couchers is officially out of beta
data.author: laurentlb
data.article_summary: Couchers平台正式推出1.0版本，脱离Beta阶段。此次发布包括新的社区安全与活跃策略，不再与竞争对手进行负面比较，并推出了全新设计的首页以更好传达平台价值。新版本还引入多项功能改进，如重新设计的地图搜索页面，加快了查找速度；更新了参考功能，允许用户提交私下安全反馈；以及新增通知中心和推送通知功能，帮助用户不漏掉重要消息。这些更新旨在提升用户体验，确保平台安全、活跃，并吸引更多新成员加入。感谢众多贡献者为此版本的付出。

44446917.article_content:
A new chapter: Couchers is officially out of Beta!
Quick summary: we are out of Beta and into version 1, we're releasing a new strategy around safe & active community instead of bashing our competitors, a fancy redesigned landing page, and a bunch of new features to make core couch surfing functionality better! Share the platform with your friends and let's grow the community together!
We are super excited to share that Couchers is today finally out of the Beta phase with our version 1 (v1) launch. After five years of building and developing the platform and community―first through the Alpha stage and a very long Beta stage―we are finally ready for our big launch! This means a brand new strategy, a spiffy new landing page, and a bunch of new features.
Today we are launching
our new strategy centered around a commitment on being the safest, healthiest, and most active couch surfing community
. This is an evolution of our
original plan
, but adapted for the next stage of the community, where we clearly define what we stand for instead of living the shadow of another platform.
In addition, we are
launching a brand new landing page
to more clearly communicate our values and what sets us apart, and to explain what our community is all about to newbies and veteran couch surfers alike.
Finally, we have combined a
number of exciting new features
into this release. These have been gradually rolled out over the past few months to make sure they are ready for you today (and hopefully mostly free of bugs)! Read on to find out what these are.
What does the v1 launch mean?
Although the platform has been usable for a long time, until now, even some of the core functionality has been somewhat buggy and not as polished as we would like, in order to call it "complete". The v1 launch signals the completion of the platform in the sense that core functionality has been cleaned up and we believe it is fully ready for all to use! A lot of this cleanup effort was also done in the
v0.9.9 release a few months ago
.
This launch means we can now focus on growing the platform and coming up with new features that set us apart and help you connect with other members better.
New Features in v1
The features we decided to work on for v1 were picked to best further our goal of being a safe and active community, as well as tighten up the core functionality of the platform to make the experience super smooth and easy.
Redesigned Landing Page
We are really excited about our
new landing page
, which clearly communicates what Couchers is, what we stand for, and what you can find on the platform once you sign up. We hope this will help us gain more of the right kinds of members!
A huge thanks to
Nicole
who built the majority of the landing page;
Pablo
and
Aapeli
who also helped build it;
Marta
and
Charlotte
who designed it;
Jesse
and
Chris
who helped test it; and countless others who helped write or brainstorm our marketing message, or provided their input in other ways!
The new landing page features an anonymized map layer: pins are randomized to be at a random point 2-10 km (1.2-6.2 mi) away from their true location and are not tied to any user info. The map is further restricted to not zoom very far in.
References
We completely overhauled functionality for leaving a reference with two key updates:
you can now indicate whether you did not stay with or host someone (and we won't remind you to leave references); and
you can now send our Safety Team private feedback (that's not shown on the public reference) about your interactions through the reference flow. You can use this functionality to let us know if something felt off, even if there's no cause for bigger concern. More information is always better and helps the Safety Team understand situations better and keep the platform safe!
Thanks to
Aapeli
,
Nicole
, and
Jason
for these updates.
Nicole
also added the number of references to the references tab on profiles to draw more attention to it.
Find members faster: a new and redesigned map
Nicole
spent months re-architecting and rebuilding a brand new Map Search page! The old one was creaking with age and very difficult to update and add features to. Nicole rewrote it from scratch!
Aapeli
helped build some new backend functionality to significantly speed up searching, and
Jesse
among many others helped test it!
We put a lot of thought into making the map as usable as possible, trying to think about what should be shown, what should be hidden, and how to best display all this data. We hope you find it useful!
Don't miss out on news: new notification feed
We've been working on notifications for quite a few releases now. In this release we introduced a notification feed, rolled out push notifications for desktop and mobile, as well as added a bunch of new notification types for things like nested replies on discussions, and pending host requests.
Don't want so many notifications? No problem. Each notification type can be adjusted for a particular it

data.title: Experiment: Colocating agent instructions with eng docs
data.author: dannyrosen
data.article_summary: 本文探讨了将AI代理指令嵌入工程师文档中的实验。作者最初对单独维护代理文档持怀疑态度，因为这可能导致信息重复和不同步。为此，作者尝试将代理指令嵌入现有的工程师文档（如`examples.rst`）的注释中，而非创建单独的文档（如`GEMINI.md`）。实验中，作者使用Gemini CLI根据文档中的指令迁移代码示例，结果显示代理严格遵循了嵌入的指令，甚至捕捉到了文档中的一个错误。尽管实验成功，但作者指出，若仓库中完全没有单独的代理文档，结果可能会有所不同。实验表明，将代理指令嵌入现有工程师文档可能是一种有效的解决方案。

主要讨论点：如何在工程项目中有效记录和利用LLM（大型语言模型）和AI助手的使用日志及指令

不同观点：
• **jauntywundrkind** 认为，默认将aider日志添加到`.gitignore`并不理想。他主张保留这些日志，以便人类和AI都能从中反思和学习。他建议将AI指令与工程文档一起保存，并提出可以利用像Backstage这样的工具来集成和管理这些知识库。他还提到了MCP服务器用于反思聊天历史的可能性，并对Kenton Varda和Cloudflare在该领域的实践表示赞赏。

• **8note** 对jauntywundrkind的观点表示支持和兴奋，特别强调了让LLM在不同工程师之间保持可重复性的重要性。他赞同保留日志和指令的想法，认为这有助于提高团队协作和知识共享的效率。

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点**：是否应该默认忽略aider日志。jauntywundrkind认为忽略日志对人类和AI都不利，而默认设置是忽略这些日志。
• **技术工具的建议**：jauntywundrkind提到了Backstage和MCP服务器的潜在应用，特别是如何通过这些工具来更好地组织和管理AI助手和LLM的使用记录。
• **实际案例**：Kenton Varda和Cloudflare的项目被当作一个好的实践例子，用于展示如何记录和推广AI指令作为参考材料。

通过这些讨论，可以看出社区对于如何在工程中有效利用和记录LLM及AI助手的使用持有不同但积极的看法，并提出了具体的工具和方法建议。

44423194.article_content:
(Experiment) Colocating agent instructions with eng docs
§
In my initial investigation of agent docs (
Docs for AI agents
) I expressed
skepticism over the current design of agent docs.  Agent providers like Claude
Code, Gemini CLI, Cursor, and so on are steering us towards maintaining agent
docs as a new docs set, separate from preexisting internal eng docs. I worry
that we’ll end up duplicating a lot of information across the two docs sets.
Inevitably, the duplicated information gets out-of-sync with each other.
In
Colocate
, I basically propose embedding the agent instructions
within the internal eng docs.  I tried out the colocate solution today, and the
results were promising. Here are the details.
Background
§
Today on
pigweed.dev
, we published
Guidelines for buildable and testable code examples
.
At the top of the page, I embedded AI agent instructions:
.. Instructions for AI agents (e.g. Gemini CLI):
.. #. Follow the workflow described in :ref:`contributing-docs-quickstart-a`.
..    Do not use Option B.
.. #. Inspect the files in ``//pw_string/examples``. This is a working example
..    of the kind of code that you need to create.
.. #. Create the code example, unit test, and build targets. The first
..    iteration of the unit test should fail.
.. #. Run ``bazelisk test //...`` to verify that your new unit test fails.
.. #. Fix the unit test.
.. #. Run ``bazelisk test //...`` again and verify that the new unit test now
..    passes.
.. _contributing-docs-examples:
===================================================
Guidelines for buildable and testable code examples
===================================================
This guide shows :ref:`docs-glossary-upstream` maintainers how to write
buildable and testable code examples for ``pigweed.dev``. It's focused on
C++ but the general pattern is theoretically applicable to any language.
…
(See
examples.rst
to view the full source code.)
All of those lines at the top of the file beginning with
..
are
comments. Humans viewing the page on a web browser don’t see those comments.
These comments are the instructions for the agent. I embedded them within
the eng doc, rather than spinning up a separate agent doc like
CLAUDE.md
,
GEMINI.md
,
AGENTS.md
, etc.
Experiment
§
I loaded up the code examples guidelines (
@docs/contributing/docs/examples.rst
)
and then instructed Gemini CLI to migrate a specific code example:
> @docs/contributing/docs/examples.rst use the instructions in examples.rst to
convert the code example in the "Known size string" section of pw_string/guide.rst
into a buildable and testable code example. Note that the examples.rst instructions
has a mistake. When you update the sphinx_docs_library Bazel rules, you should
update the `srcs` list, not the `deps` list.
Results
§
It worked really well. Gemini CLI closely followed the agent instructions
that I provided. Specifically:
I told Gemini CLI to first create a failing test, verify that the test fails,
and then fix it. It did exactly that.
I got inadvertent confirmation that Gemini CLI was following my instructions
closely. There’s a mistake in
examples.rst
. It instructs you to update
the
deps
list in the
sphinx_docs_library
. You actually need to update
the
srcs
list. The first time I tried this workflow, Gemini CLI got
confused because it could not find a
deps
list on the rule.
Caveats:
This was an informal experiment. To properly control the experiment, the
repo should have no agent docs, i.e. no
GEMINI.md
files. This was not
the case. The Pigweed repo has an extensive agent doc, as you can see in
the logs after I run the
/memory
show
command. So, it’s still not clear
whether the agent would successfully complete the task if given only colocated
instructions. In other words, maybe this experiment is suggesting that you
get the best results when you have both agent docs and more targeted
instructions.
Below is the full log. See
pwrev.dev/301461/1
to view the code that Gemini CLI
generated.
kayce@kayce0 ~/p/pigweed (main)> gemini
███            █████████  ██████████ ██████   ██████ █████ ██████   █████ █████
░░░███         ███░░░░░███░░███░░░░░█░░██████ ██████ ░░███ ░░██████ ░░███ ░░███

data.title: My open source project was relicensed by a YC company [license updated]
data.author: sohzm
data.article_summary: 文章指出，在x.com网站上，某些与隐私相关的浏览器扩展程序可能会引发问题。建议用户禁用这些扩展程序，然后重试访问该网站。文章提醒用户不必担心，可以尝试再次操作。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：开源代码的许可、使用和侵权问题，特别是在一个涉及作弊工具的项目中。

不同观点：
• **fargle**：认为开源代码不能被"偷"。开源代码的再利用和商业化并不构成盗窃，只要使用的是不兼容的许可证。这里的重点是许可证的合法性问题，以及开源项目被商业化的合理性。

• **tombert**：对开源感到失望，特别是GPL许可证的执行难度。认为公司可能通过销售优化后的二进制文件来规避GPL，且难以证明侵权行为。这反映了开源开发者在维权方面的无奈和困境。

• **VoidWhisperer**：虽然认为开源代码的盗用是不对的，但对具体案例（作弊工具）并不感到同情。这表明对特定类型项目的道德判断影响了其对版权问题的看法。

• **litexlang**：对开源项目的困难表示同情，并建议通过社区支持来反击侵权行为。强调开源社区的团结和支持。

• **nativeit**：质疑原项目的合法性和正当性，因为项目涉及作弊工具。并指出代码相似性可能仅仅是由于类似的想法和使用类似的技术，而非直接的抄袭。

• **an0malous**：提到一些知名公司通过利用法律和道德的灰色地带取得成功，暗示这种情况在科技行业并不少见。

• **kratoskr221**：关注此类侵权行为对开源社区的负面影响，并询问是否可以通过法律手段解决此类问题，以保护开源开发者的权益。

补充讨论：
• **alberth**：提到相关的代码库似乎是GPL-3许可，或者曾经是，可能涉及到许可证的变更或重新许可问题。

• **sohzm**：简短回应，似乎承认项目的价值有限，但仍代表了一定的努力。

• **bhouston**：幽默地指出，作弊工具被另一个从事类似业务的公司盗用，具有一定的讽刺意味。

• **InkCanon 和 kevbin**：简短评论，涉及到对项目作者身份的猜测和双方可能合作的可能性。

争议焦点：
• 开源代码的再利用和商业化是否构成盗窃，特别是在许可证不兼容的情况下。
• 涉及不道德用途（如作弊工具）的开源项目是否值得同情和保护。
• 如何有效保护和维权开源项目的版权，特别是在代码被修改和重新发布的情况下。

data.title: 'Kill Bill: The Whole Bloody Affair' in 35mm – Dir's Cut 258min and Intermission
data.author: andsoitis
data.article_summary: 这个夏天，由奥斯卡获奖导演昆汀·塔伦蒂诺拥有的维斯塔剧院将放映《杀死比尔》的加长版《Kill Bill: The Whole Bloody Affair》。这部时长258分钟的导演剪辑版将于7月18日至28日在大银幕上以35毫米格式放映。该版本曾在2006年戛纳电影节上亮相，包含法语字幕和中场休息，是塔伦蒂诺最初为观众设想的完整版。与原版电影相比，这个版本包含一些不同的镜头，如仅在日本版中出现的画面、编辑过的悬念和附加的动画片段。门票现已开始预售，票价为21美元。放映地点为维斯塔剧院，时间为7月18日至28日，每天有12:30和19:30两场放映。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对某部影片（从评论内容推测为某分为上下两部或多部的影片）的不同卷的评价，特别是对黑白画面与彩色画面的效果对比以及整体观感。

不同观点：
• 观点一：评论者[wodenokoto]认为影片的黑白画面很酷，并且对彩色画面效果持怀疑态度，不确定彩色版本是否能带来同样的观感。这表明评论者对黑白画面有特别的欣赏，同时暗示黑白和彩色可能带来不同的情感体验。

• 观点二：评论者对两部卷的感受存在明显差异。他认为第一卷非常精彩，甚至是其最爱的电影之一，而第二卷则显得无聊。这表明影片的内容或者节奏在不同卷之间可能存在较大的变化，导致观感上的不同。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：影片的第二卷是否真的无聊。评论者明确表达了对第二卷的失望，但这可能只是个人感受，其他观众可能会有不同的看法。这涉及到观众对影片节奏、剧情发展等方面的期待差异。

• 另一个值得注意的点是评论者对黑白与彩色画面的比较，提出了视觉效果对观影体验的影响，可能引发其他观众对影片艺术风格的讨论。这涉及到电影艺术表现手法（如色彩运用）如何影响观众的感受与评价。

Vista Theater
, the iconic Hollywood theater
owned by
Oscar-winning director
Quentin Tarantino
, is screening an extended version of
Kill Bill
this summer!
Kill Bill: The Whole Bloody Affair
,
the 258-minute
director’s cut
of the iconic action films, is set to
play on the big screen and in 35mm
from July 18 through July 28th.
The
four-and-a-half-hour “unrated epic”
originally played at the Cannes Film Festival in 2006, complete with French subtitles and an intermission, and is the version Tarantino originally intended for audiences. The film was cut down into two movies, hence Vol. 1 and Vol. 2 in the original film’s titles.
View this post on Instagram
A post shared by Vista Theater Hollywood (@vistatheaterhollywood)
What’s different in this version of the film?
According to
The Quentin Tarantino Archives
,
The Whole Bloody Affair
has notable differences
from the original films, including shots seen only in
Kill Bill
‘s Japanese release, edited cliffhangers and tags, and additional anime sequences.
“We’ve actually added some things to it,”
said Tarantino
back in 2009
. “We did a whole little chapter that I wrote and designed for the animated sequence, that we never did, because we figured, back when it was gonna be one big movie, it was going to be too long, so we didn’t do it. So when we were talking about re-releasing it, they asked is there anything you can put in, and I said no I put everything in there, but… there’s one sequence that we wouldn’t even have to shoot! So we got together with Production IG and did it, and it’s really cool. So it’s this little seven-minute sequence, it’s really cool, it’s in the O-Ren chapter.”
Advance tickets on sale now
at the theater and
online
, and are $21 with fees.

data.author: Arubis

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：欧洲与美国之间技术工作者移民、薪资和生活质量的比较

不同观点：
• [0xfaded] 认为如果在欧洲找到一份薪资高于平均水平的工作，移民到理想的欧洲国家并不难，尤其是对技术工作者来说。他建议先在美国赚钱，然后为了更好的生活质量或价值观迁移到欧洲。他还提到迁移财富时可能遇到的税务问题（如退出税）。
   
• [drdunce] 持相反观点，认为欧盟的科技人才市场已经饱和，对高需求技术专业人士的需求不大。

• [j7ake] 质疑为什么只关注科技行业，建议寻找欧盟薪资比美国更好的其他行业。

• [ldjkfkdsjnv] 回应[j7ake]的评论，提到外包公司如Wipro、Infosys、Cognizant是可能的选项，但暗示这些工作的薪资低且内容乏味。

• [android521] 同意[ldjkfkdsjnv]的观点，进一步指出这些工作不仅薪资低，而且工作内容无趣。

• [throwawaysleep] 认为对于研究型人才，欧盟有更大的机会，并指出直到今年人们还主要从欧盟流向美国。

• [keiferski] 提到Nomad Capitalist这个人正在实践这种迁移策略。

• [scarface_74] 质疑为什么要去薪资低、税高、生活成本却不低的国家，认为没有足够的理由离开美国。

• [dmitrygr] 支持[scarface_74]的观点，认为找到薪资和美国一样高、且生活质量更好的地方不容易，并指出离开美国的决定说起来容易，做起来难。

补充讨论：
• 评论中多次提到迁移财富时的税务问题，特别是“退出税”，这是迁移过程中的一个实际障碍。
• 不同评论者对欧盟科技人才市场的供需情况有不同看法，有的认为市场饱和，有的则认为对特定人才仍有需求。
• 对工作内容和薪资的讨论，尤其是外包公司的工作，显示出对某些职位的负面看法。
• 总体而言，评论反映了对生活质量、价值观和薪资之间权衡的复杂考虑。
